concepts.statement: Under the Hartree approximation the N-electron problem separates into one-electron Schrödinger equations, −(ħ²/2m)∇²ψ_i + V(r)ψ_i = ε_iψ_i, where V is the nucleus's potential plus the mean field of the other electrons.

concepts.name: Coulomb integral
concepts.statement: The six-dimensional integral J_{j,k} = ∫|φ_j(r)|²|φ_k(r′)|² e²/|r − r′| dr dr′, the Coulomb repulsion between the charge densities of an electron in φ_j and one in φ_k.

concepts.name: Orbital energy in the Hartree approximation
concepts.statement: The energy of orbital φ_j is the sum of its kinetic energy, its attraction to the nucleus and its Coulomb repulsion with the electrons in every other occupied orbital (k ≠ j, so the electron does not repel itself).

concepts.name: Self-consistent field method
concepts.statement: The iterative solution of nonlinear one-electron equations whose potential depends on their own solutions: guess the orbitals, build the charge density and the potential, solve for new orbitals, and repeat until the density no longer changes.

concepts.name: Limits of the screening model
concepts.statement: Hydrogen-like orbitals with a screened nuclear charge Z_eff describe atoms only qualitatively: their energies do not match measured ionization energies and miss the trends in orbital energies, such as 4s lying below 3d in potassium and calcium and above it from scandium on.

concepts.name: Magnetic field
concepts.statement: The field set up by moving charges, measured in gauss or tesla (1 T = 10⁴ G), which exerts a torque on a magnetic dipole and shifts its energy.

concepts.name: Magnetic dipole moment
concepts.statement: The vector μ_m that a circulating charge carries because of its angular momentum, like a small bar magnet; an electron's orbital or spin motion gives it one.

concepts.name: Energy of a magnetic dipole in a field
concepts.statement: A magnetic dipole in a magnetic field has the energy E_B = −μ_m · B: lowest with the moment along the field, highest against it.

concepts.name: Gyromagnetic ratio
concepts.statement: The constant γ that relates a magnetic moment to the angular momentum that produces it, μ = γL; for the orbital motion of an electron it is γ_e = −e/2m_e.

concepts.name: Bohr magneton
concepts.statement: The fundamental magnetic moment μ_B = eħ/2m_e = −γ_eħ = 9.2732 × 10⁻²⁴ J/T (9.2732 × 10⁻²¹ erg/G), which converts a magnetic field into an energy for any particle with the electron's charge and mass.

concepts.name: Zeeman energy
concepts.statement: In a field B_z a hydrogen state's energy shifts in proportion to its magnetic quantum number, ⟨E⟩ = E_n + μ_B B_z m_l, so the field lifts the m_l degeneracy: a 2p level splits into three and its emission line into three.

concepts.name: Electron spin
concepts.statement: The electron has an intrinsic angular momentum, its spin, with a magnetic moment of its own; it is postulated to explain experiments such as the microwave absorption of hydrogen and the Stern–Gerlach splitting, and it is not the rotation of a charged ball.

concepts.name: Stern–Gerlach experiment
concepts.statement: A beam of silver atoms sent through an inhomogeneous magnetic field splits into two beams, not a spread, because the atom's one unpaired electron has a spin moment whose component along the field takes only two values.

concepts.name: Spin angular momentum
concepts.statement: The angular momentum vector S of the electron's spin, defined by analogy with the orbital angular momentum L and described by spin operators with the same properties.

concepts.name: Spin operators
concepts.statement: The operators Ŝ² and Ŝ_z of the spin angular momentum, built with the properties of L̂² and L̂_z.

concepts.name: Spin quantum number
concepts.statement: The quantum number s that fixes the magnitude of the spin angular momentum through Ŝ²σ = s(s + 1)ħ²σ, playing the part l plays for orbital motion.

concepts.name: Spin magnetic quantum number
concepts.statement: The fourth quantum number m_s, the projection of the spin on the z axis in units of ħ, which runs from −s to +s in integer steps.

concepts.name: Spin eigenvalue equations
concepts.statement: Spin states are eigenfunctions of Ŝ² with eigenvalue s(s + 1)ħ² and of Ŝ_z with eigenvalue m_sħ, so the z component of spin is S_z = m_sħ.

concepts.name: The electron's spin is one half
concepts.statement: One observed transition means two spin states, m_s = +s and −s, one integer step apart, so 2s = 1 and s = ½: m_s is +½ or −½.

concepts.name: Spin states α and β
concepts.statement: The two spin wavefunctions of an electron: α with m_s = +½ (S_z = +ħ/2) and β with m_s = −½ (S_z = −ħ/2); their functional form is unknown, and they are taken to be normalized and orthogonal over the spin variable.

concepts.name: Electron spin resonance
concepts.statement: Hydrogen atoms in their ground state absorb microwaves in a magnetic field, at 28 GHz in 10⁴ G and at a frequency proportional to the field: the field splits two spin states of equal energy, and a photon is absorbed when hν = E_α − E_β.

concepts.name: Spin gyromagnetic ratio
concepts.statement: The constant γ_s relating the spin magnetic moment to the spin angular momentum, μ_s = γ_s S.

concepts.name: Electron g-factor
concepts.statement: The microwave line gives hν/B = −γ_sħ, about twice the Bohr magneton: γ_s = 2.0023γ_e. The factor g = 2.0023 for a free electron measures how far the spin's moment-to-angular-momentum ratio departs from the orbital one; Dirac's relativistic theory predicts it.

concepts.name: Indistinguishability of identical particles
concepts.statement: Identical particles such as electrons cannot be told apart by any experiment, so a description of them may not depend on labels: the probability density must be unchanged when two of them are interchanged.

concepts.name: Spin-orbital
concepts.statement: A one-electron wavefunction with both a spatial part (an orbital, set by n, l and m_l) and a spin part (α or β, set by m_s).

concepts.name: Exchange changes a wavefunction by ±1
concepts.statement: Interchanging two identical particles may change the wavefunction only by a phase e^{iφ}; doing it twice restores the original, so e^{2iφ} = 1 and the factor is +1 or −1.

concepts.name: Exchange operator
concepts.statement: The operator P̂₁₂ that swaps the labels of particles 1 and 2 in a many-particle wavefunction; it commutes with any physical Hamiltonian, and its eigenvalues are +1 and −1.

concepts.name: Permutation symmetry
concepts.statement: A wavefunction is symmetric when interchanging two particles leaves it unchanged (eigenvalue +1 of P̂₁₂) and antisymmetric when the interchange changes its sign (eigenvalue −1).

concepts.name: Boson
concepts.statement: A particle of integer spin, such as a photon or a deuterium nucleus, whose many-particle wavefunction is symmetric to interchange.

concepts.name: Fermion
concepts.statement: A particle of half-integer spin, such as an electron, proton or neutrino, whose many-particle wavefunction is antisymmetric to interchange.

concepts.name: Antisymmetry of electronic wavefunctions
concepts.statement: Because electrons are fermions, every wavefunction of several electrons must change sign when any two of them are interchanged, including one built from single-electron functions.

concepts.name: Antisymmetric two-electron wavefunction
concepts.statement: A simple product of two spin-orbitals is neither symmetric nor antisymmetric; the antisymmetric combination is ψ⁻ = (1/√2)[φ_a(1)φ_b(2) − φ_a(2)φ_b(1)], while the symmetric ones may also put both particles in one state.

concepts.name: Pauli exclusion principle
concepts.statement: No two electrons can be described by the same spin-orbital: if φ_a = φ_b the antisymmetric combination vanishes, so an orbital holds at most two electrons, of opposite spin, and no two electrons share all four quantum numbers.

concepts.name: Electron configuration
concepts.statement: The list of the orbitals an atom's electrons occupy with how many in each, written like 1s²2s⁰2p⁰ for ground-state helium or 1s²2s²2p² for carbon.

concepts.name: Microstate
concepts.statement: One particular way of placing the electrons of a configuration in its spin-orbitals, drawn as a diagram with each electron's orbital and spin; the 1s¹2s¹ configuration of helium has four.

concepts.name: Spatial and spin parts of two-electron wavefunctions
concepts.statement: A two-electron wavefunction can often be written as a spatial part times a spin part, one symmetric and the other antisymmetric: ground-state helium is 1s(1)1s(2) times (1/√2)[α(1)β(2) − α(2)β(1)], and the 1s¹2s¹ states pair the antisymmetric spatial function with the three symmetric spin functions αα, αβ + βα and ββ, and the symmetric one with αβ − βα.

concepts.name: Slater determinant
concepts.statement: An antisymmetric N-electron wavefunction written as a determinant of spin-orbitals, one row per electron and one column per spin-orbital, normalized by 1/√N!; expanded it has N! terms.

concepts.name: Antisymmetry of a Slater determinant
concepts.statement: Interchanging two electrons interchanges two rows of the determinant and changes its sign, so a Slater determinant is antisymmetric by construction, and two identical columns (one spin-orbital used twice) make it vanish.

concepts.name: Combinations of Slater determinants
concepts.statement: One Slater determinant corresponds to one microstate diagram; where a state cannot be written as a spatial part times a spin part, as for two of helium's 1s¹2s¹ states, it is a combination of determinants, ψ₁ ∝ φ_a − φ_c and ψ₃ ∝ φ_a + φ_c.

concepts.name: Hartree–Fock method
concepts.statement: Fock's improvement of the Hartree method: the wavefunction is a Slater determinant of spin-orbitals, so it is antisymmetric, and the variational principle then gives one-electron equations that carry an exchange term besides the Hartree terms; they are solved by the self-consistent field method.

concepts.name: Exchange integral
concepts.statement: The two-electron integral K_{i,j} that resembles the Coulomb integral with the electrons' labels interchanged in one orbital pair; it arises only between electrons of the same spin and lowers their repulsion.

concepts.name: Hartree–Fock equations
concepts.statement: N one-electron equations: kinetic energy, attraction to the nucleus and the Hartree (Coulomb) term as in the Hartree equations, minus an exchange term that acts only between electrons of the same spin and keeps them apart.

concepts.name: Fock operator
concepts.statement: The one-electron operator F̂ = Ĥ⁰ + Σ_j(2Ĵ_j − K̂_j) whose eigenfunctions are the Hartree–Fock orbitals: the hydrogen-like operator plus Coulomb and exchange operators built from every occupied orbital, so F̂φ_i = ε_iφ_i must be solved iteratively.

concepts.name: Exchange interaction
concepts.statement: A quantum effect between identical particles that comes from the symmetry of their wavefunction under exchange, not a true force: for fermions it acts as a repulsion of like spins (Pauli repulsion), for bosons as an attraction.

concepts.name: Hartree–Fock orbital energy
concepts.statement: ε_i is the kinetic and nuclear-attraction energy of an electron in φ_i plus its Coulomb-minus-exchange interaction with the electrons in all the occupied spin-orbitals; for an occupied orbital the j = i term cancels, so ε_i counts N − 1 partners.

concepts.name: Virtual orbital
concepts.statement: An unoccupied Hartree–Fock spin-orbital; its energy counts interactions with all N occupied spin-orbitals, so it describes an electron added to an N-electron system.

concepts.name: Hartree–Fock energy
concepts.statement: The total energy of the best single-determinant wavefunction, the lowest the complete Hamiltonian gives for any such function; it reaches about 99% of the experimental energy (helium −5.72 against −5.80 R_H) and misses the electron correlation.

concepts.name: Frozen-orbital approximation
concepts.statement: Removing or adding an electron without re-optimizing the other spin-orbitals, so the parent's Hartree–Fock orbitals describe the ion as well; it neglects orbital relaxation.

concepts.name: Koopmans' theorem
concepts.statement: Within the frozen-orbital model the ionization energy is minus the energy of the occupied spin-orbital emptied, E_{N−1} − E_N = −ε_k, and the electron affinity is minus the energy of the virtual one filled, E_N − E_{N+1} = −ε_k; the estimates are often within about 0.5 eV.

concepts.name: Exchange hole
concepts.statement: Around an electron the density of other electrons with the same spin is reduced: the Hartree approximation gives a structureless conditional density, while the antisymmetric Hartree–Fock wavefunction carves a hole near r = 0; electrons of opposite spin are unaffected.

concepts.name: Closed and open shells
concepts.statement: A completely filled subshell is closed: its electrons' orbital and spin angular momenta cancel, so only the electrons of partly filled (open) subshells set an atom's state.

concepts.name: Total orbital angular momentum quantum number
concepts.statement: The quantum number L of the orbital angular momenta of an atom's electrons added as vectors, from l₁ + l₂ down to |l₁ − l₂| in integer steps for two electrons.

concepts.name: Total magnetic quantum number
concepts.statement: M_l, the total z component of the electrons' orbital angular momentum, the sum of their m_l, which can be negative and runs from m_{l1} + m_{l2} down to its negative.

concepts.name: Total spin magnetic quantum number
concepts.statement: M_s, the total z component of the electrons' spins, the sum of their m_s: 1, 0 or −1 for two electrons.

concepts.name: Total spin quantum number
concepts.statement: S, the quantum number of the resultant of all the electrons' spin vectors, never negative: S = s₁ + s₂, …, |s₁ − s₂|, so 1 or 0 for two open-shell electrons and 3/2 or ½ for three.

concepts.name: Total angular momentum quantum number
concepts.statement: J, the quantum number of the total angular momentum formed by combining the total orbital and total spin angular momenta, from L + S down to |L − S|.

concepts.name: Spin multiplicity
concepts.statement: The number 2S + 1 of spin states of a level: a singlet (S = 0) has one, a doublet (S = ½) two and a triplet (S = 1) three, since two electron spins combine to S = 1 in three ways and to S = 0 in one.

concepts.name: Term symbol
concepts.statement: The label ^{2S+1}L_J of an atomic energy level: the code letter S, P, D, F, G, H for L = 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, the multiplicity as a left superscript and J as a right subscript; a closed-shell atom is ¹S₀.

concepts.name: Finding the terms of a configuration
concepts.statement: Tabulating every microstate of the open-shell electrons by M_l and M_s, then repeatedly taking the largest remaining M_l and claiming a centred block of the table for one term (a ¹G takes M_l = 4 to −4 at M_s = 0, a ³F takes M_l = 3 to −3 at all three M_s), until nothing is left.

concepts.name: Hund's rules
concepts.statement: Empirical rules that order the terms of a configuration and reliably give its ground term: the highest multiplicity lies lowest; among equal multiplicities, the highest L; then for a subshell less than half full the lowest J, and for one more than half full the highest J.

concepts.name: Electrons and holes give the same terms
concepts.statement: A subshell missing k electrons has the same terms as one holding k: p¹ and p⁵ alike, p² and p⁴ alike, and so for d and f.

concepts.name: L–S coupling
concepts.statement: Russell–Saunders coupling, used for the lighter elements: the electrons' orbital angular momenta add to L and their spins to S, and then L and S add to the total J.

concepts.name: j–j coupling
concepts.statement: The coupling scheme for heavy elements (Z above about 40): each electron's orbital and spin angular momenta first combine to its own j, and the j add to J; there L and S stop being good quantum numbers.

concepts.name: Spin–orbit interaction
concepts.statement: The magnetic interaction of an electron's spin moment with the moment of its orbital motion, proportional to S · L; because of it L and S no longer commute with the Hamiltonian separately, but J does and is conserved.

concepts.name: Magnitudes and projections of L, S and J
concepts.statement: Each angular momentum has magnitude ħ√(q(q + 1)) and z projection m_qħ: |L| = ħ√(l(l + 1)) with L_z = m_lħ, |S| = ħ√(s(s + 1)) with S_z = m_sħ, |J| = ħ√(j(j + 1)) with J_z = m_jħ, and m_j = m_l + m_s.

concepts.name: Degeneracy of a term
concepts.statement: A level ^{2S+1}L_J is 2J + 1-fold degenerate, one state for each z projection m_J from +J to −J; hydrogen's ²S₁/₂ ground state is two-fold.

concepts.name: Aufbau principle
concepts.statement: Electrons fill the lowest-energy orbitals first and move to higher ones only when the lower ones are full; it does not say how to fill orbitals of equal energy.

concepts.name: Why parallel spins lie lowest
concepts.statement: Putting two electrons in separate orbitals removes the Coulomb repulsion of sharing one, and giving them parallel spins gains the favorable exchange energy, which grows with the number of possible exchanges between electrons of the same spin.

concepts.name: Finding a ground-state term symbol
concepts.statement: Applying Hund's rules to a configuration in turn: maximize S, then L, then pick J = |L − S| for a subshell less than half full or J = L + S for one more than half full.

concepts.name: Fine structure
concepts.statement: The splitting of a spectral line into a multiplet of closely spaced lines (a doublet, a triplet) by spin–orbit coupling and relativistic effects; hydrogen's Hα line is a doublet 0.326 cm⁻¹ apart.

concepts.name: One-electron selection rules
concepts.statement: When light moves one electron between atomic orbitals, Δl = ±1 and Δm_l = 0, ±1, because the photon carries one unit of angular momentum.

concepts.name: Russell–Saunders selection rules
concepts.statement: In L–S coupling an allowed transition has ΔS = 0, ΔL = 0, ±1 and ΔJ = 0, ±1 (not J = 0 to 0), with Δm_J = 0, ±1 (not 0 to 0 when ΔJ = 0); they fail in heavy atoms, where singlet–triplet lines are seen.

concepts.name: Fine structure of hydrogen's n = 2 and n = 3 levels
concepts.statement: Hydrogen's n = 2 level holds the terms ²S₁/₂, ²P₁/₂ and ²P₃/₂ (8 states) and n = 3 five terms (18 states); terms of the same n and J have the same energy, and of the five allowed 3 → 2 transitions two strong ones make the Hα doublet, 0.364 − 0.036 = 0.328 cm⁻¹ apart against 0.326 cm⁻¹ measured.

concepts.name: Sodium D lines
concepts.statement: Sodium's yellow D line is a doublet, D₁ at 589.6 nm and D₂ at 589.0 nm, because the 3p level of its one valence electron splits by spin–orbit coupling into ²P₁/₂ and ²P₃/₂; every line ending or starting on 3p is doubled the same way.

concepts.name: Quantum chemistry
concepts.statement: The use of quantum mechanics to predict the bonding patterns, geometries and properties of molecules. For all but the simplest molecules exact solutions of the Schrödinger equation are not available, so its methods and software packages rest on a series of approximations.

concepts.name: Internuclear distance
concepts.statement: The distance R between the two nuclei of a diatomic molecule, the coordinate on which its electronic energy and wavefunction depend.

concepts.name: Hamiltonian of a diatomic molecule
concepts.statement: The Hamiltonian of a diatomic molecule grouped into three terms: the kinetic energy of the nuclei, the Coulomb repulsion Z_AZ_Be²/4πε₀R of the two nuclei, and the electronic Hamiltonian, which holds the electrons' kinetic energy, their mutual repulsion and their attraction to the nuclei.

concepts.name: Electronic Hamiltonian
concepts.statement: The part Ĥ_elec of a molecule's Hamiltonian that holds the electrons' kinetic energy, their attraction to each nucleus and their repulsion for each other, for nuclei at fixed positions R; the factor ½ keeps each pair of electrons from being counted twice.

concepts.name: Born–Oppenheimer approximation
concepts.statement: A nucleus is more than a thousand times heavier than an electron, so the nuclei move slowly while the electrons respond to forces almost at once. The approximation neglects the nuclear kinetic energy in solving for the electrons, which are described with the nuclei held still at each position R, separating the motion of the electrons from that of the nuclei.

concepts.name: Electronic Schrödinger equation
concepts.statement: Within the Born–Oppenheimer approximation the electronic wavefunction φ_e(r, R) and the electronic energy E_e(R) solve Ĥ_elec φ_e = E_e(R) φ_e, once for each fixed position of the nuclei; both depend on R although the nuclear motion is neglected.

concepts.name: Born–Oppenheimer wavefunction
concepts.statement: The molecular wavefunction as a product ψ_ne(r, R) = X_ne(R)φ_e(r, R) of a vibrational wavefunction of the nuclear coordinates, which depends on both the vibrational and the electronic state, and the electronic wavefunction; translational and rotational wavefunctions multiply it where those motions are not coupled to it.

concepts.name: Potential energy curve
concepts.statement: The electronic energy plus the Coulomb repulsion of the nuclei, V_e(R) = E_e(R) + Z_AZ_Be²/4πε₀R: the energy of a diatomic molecule against the internuclear separation, which is the potential energy of the nuclei. Large and positive at very small R, it falls to a minimum where a bond forms and levels off at large R to two weakly interacting atoms.

concepts.name: Equilibrium bond length
concepts.statement: The internuclear separation R₀ at which the potential energy curve has its minimum: the equilibrium position of the nuclei.

concepts.name: Crude Born–Oppenheimer approximation
concepts.statement: A further simplification in which R is set to the equilibrium separation R₀ and the electronic wavefunction found there is used for every position of the nuclei, as if the nuclei never moved.

concepts.name: Nuclear Schrödinger equation
concepts.statement: The potential energy curve controls the motion of the nuclei: (T̂_nuc + V(R))X_ne = E_ne X_ne gives the vibrational wavefunctions and energies, for which the harmonic or the Morse potential is an approximation to V(R).

concepts.name: Potential energy surface
concepts.statement: The energy of a molecule of more than two atoms as a function of its 3N − 6 internal coordinates (3N − 5 for a linear molecule), the many-dimensional counterpart of a diatomic's potential energy curve; its minimum is the molecule's equilibrium shape.

concepts.name: Reaction coordinate diagram
concepts.statement: A one-dimensional slice through a potential energy surface, which chemists use to rationalize and illustrate how the potential energy varies with molecular motion in a reaction or process.

concepts.name: Hydrogen molecular ion
concepts.statement: H₂⁺, two protons held together by one electron, the simplest conceivable molecule. Its Schrödinger equation can be solved exactly within the Born–Oppenheimer approximation, which makes it the prototype for diatomic bonding as the hydrogen atom is for atomic structure.

concepts.name: Electronic Hamiltonian of H₂⁺
concepts.statement: The electronic Hamiltonian of H₂⁺: the electron's kinetic energy, its attraction to protons A and B at distances r_A and r_B, and the repulsion of the two protons a distance R apart.

concepts.name: Molecular orbital
concepts.statement: A one-electron wavefunction that extends over the whole molecule, the counterpart of an atomic orbital in the orbital description of a molecule.

concepts.name: LCAO-MO method
terms: Linear Combination of Atomic Orbitals - Molecular Orbital (LCAO-MO) Method
concepts.statement: Finding molecular orbitals as linear combinations of atomic orbitals, the linear variational method with the atomic orbitals of the molecule's atoms as the basis. For H₂⁺ the basis is the two hydrogen 1s orbitals, ψ = C_A1s_A + C_B1s_B; in general |ψ_J⟩ = Σ_i c_{J,i}|φ_i⟩.

concepts.name: Number of molecular orbitals
concepts.statement: The secular determinant of a basis of N atomic orbitals has N roots, so a molecule has as many molecular orbitals as there are atomic orbitals in the basis: two 1s orbitals give two molecular orbitals.

concepts.name: Interference of atomic orbitals
concepts.statement: Two atomic orbitals added with the same sign reinforce each other, as two waves interfere constructively, and the electron density between the nuclei increases; subtracted, they interfere destructively and leave a node between the nuclei.

concepts.name: Molecular orbitals of H₂⁺
concepts.statement: Since the two protons are identical, the electron is as likely near one as near the other, |C_A|² = |C_B|², which gives two molecular orbitals, ψ₊ = C₊(1s_A + 1s_B) and ψ₋ = C₋(1s_A − 1s_B). The charge density of ψ₊ is enhanced between the protons; ψ₋ has a node in the middle.

concepts.name: Bonding molecular orbital
concepts.statement: A molecular orbital whose electron density is enhanced between the nuclei, which holds them together against their repulsion; for H₂⁺ it is ψ₊, the sum of the two 1s orbitals.

concepts.name: Antibonding molecular orbital
concepts.statement: A molecular orbital with little electron density between the nuclei and a node there, which cannot balance their repulsion; for H₂⁺ it is ψ₋, the difference of the two 1s orbitals.

concepts.name: Normalized molecular orbitals of H₂⁺
concepts.statement: Normalizing ψ± with the overlap integral S = ⟨1s_A|1s_B⟩ of the real 1s orbitals gives |C±|²(2 ± 2S) = 1, so C± = 1/√(2(1 ± S)) and ψ± = (1s_A ± 1s_B)/√(2(1 ± S)).

concepts.name: Overlap integral of two 1s orbitals
concepts.statement: For two hydrogen 1s orbitals a distance R apart, S(R) = e^{−R/a₀}(1 + R/a₀ + R²/3a₀²): 1 when the nuclei coincide and the two functions are the same, falling toward 0 as the nuclei separate and the functions stop overlapping.

concepts.name: LCAO energies of H₂⁺
concepts.statement: The expectation value of Ĥ_elec in ψ± is E± = [H_AA + H_BB ± H_AB ± H_BA]/2(1 ± S). Protons A and B enter the Hamiltonian equivalently, so H_AA = H_BB, and the orbitals are real, so H_AB = H_BA, which leaves E± = (H_AA ± H_AB)/(1 ± S).

concepts.name: Coulomb integral of H₂⁺
concepts.statement: J = ⟨1s_A|−e²/4πε₀r_B|1s_A⟩, the average potential energy of the electron density around proton A in the field of proton B: the attraction of proton B to hydrogen atom A's electron density. It is negative and goes to zero as the protons separate.

concepts.name: Overlap charge density
concepts.statement: The product eφ*_{1s_A}φ_{1s_B}, which is significant only where the two atomic orbitals overlap, in the region between the nuclei, and so contributes to the chemical bond.

concepts.name: Exchange integral of H₂⁺
concepts.statement: K = ⟨1s_A|−e²/4πε₀r_A|1s_B⟩, with the electron in 1s_A on one side of the operator and in 1s_B on the other: the potential energy of the overlap charge density with one of the protons, the added attraction from the charge built up between them. It is negative and goes to zero as the protons separate.

concepts.name: Energy of H₂⁺ against proton separation
concepts.statement: With H_AA = E_H + e²/4πε₀R + J and H_AB = (E_H + e²/4πε₀R)S + K, the energy is E± = E_H + e²/4πε₀R + (J ± K)/(1 ± S): a hydrogen atom, the protons' repulsion and the electron's added interactions with the protons. Measured from a separated hydrogen atom and proton, ΔE± = e²/4πε₀R + (J ± K)/(1 ± S).

concepts.name: Stability of the H₂⁺ bond
concepts.statement: A bond forms where ΔE is negative and has a minimum, so (J ± K)/(1 ± S) must outweigh the protons' repulsion at some R. For ψ₊, J and K together do, and the energy has a minimum near R = 2.5a₀; for ψ₋, −K nearly cancels J and the energy is always above that of the separated atom and proton. S has only a small effect.

concepts.name: Sigma orbital
concepts.statement: A molecular orbital whose electron density has cylindrical symmetry about the internuclear axis: every cross-section perpendicular to the axis is a circle. σ_1s, the sum of two 1s orbitals, is a bonding σ orbital, and σ*_1s, their difference, the antibonding one.

concepts.name: Nodal plane of an antibonding orbital
concepts.statement: Antibonding orbitals contain a node, a plane of zero electron density, perpendicular to the internuclear axis; bonding orbitals do not.

concepts.name: Molecular orbital energy-level diagram
concepts.statement: A schematic drawing that compares the energies of the molecular orbitals (bonding, antibonding and nonbonding) with the energies of the parent atomic orbitals.

concepts.name: Stabilization of bonding orbitals
concepts.statement: Electrons in a bonding orbital interact with both nuclei at once, so a bonding molecular orbital is always lower in energy, more stable, than its component atomic orbitals; electrons in an antibonding orbital interact with one nucleus at a time and lie farther from it, so an antibonding orbital is always higher.

concepts.name: Larger LCAO basis sets
concepts.statement: The 1s-only LCAO picture of H₂⁺ gives a bond length of 134 pm and a dissociation energy of 1.8 eV against 106 pm and 2.8 eV exact, because spherical 1s orbitals cannot favour the space between the nuclei. Adding orbitals such as 2s and 2p_z on each atom gives the linear variational method more coefficients, a lower energy and a better charge density.

concepts.name: Molecular electron configuration
concepts.statement: The molecular orbitals a molecule's electrons occupy and how many are in each. By the Aufbau and Pauli principles two electrons of opposite spin go into each spatial orbital in order of increasing energy, so the ground state of a 2n-electron molecule is ψ₁²ψ₂²…ψ_n²; higher-energy configurations give excited states.

concepts.name: Symmetry labels of molecular orbitals
concepts.statement: A diatomic molecule keeps a component of angular momentum along its axis, which labels its orbitals: σ means a component of 0 and no node in any plane containing the axis, π a node in such a plane and a wavefunction antisymmetric to reflection in it. A prefix numbers the orbitals of a type and a superscript gives their electrons, as in 2σ_g².

concepts.name: Gerade and ungerade
concepts.statement: A homonuclear diatomic molecule has a center of inversion in the middle of the bond, and its orbitals are either g (gerade), ψ(x, y, z) = ψ(−x, −y, −z) about that center, or u (ungerade), changing sign under inversion. A heteronuclear diatomic has no center of inversion and no g or u label.

concepts.name: Hierarchy of quantum chemistry methods
concepts.statement: LCAO only chooses the mixing coefficients of orbitals assumed to be atomic and gives qualitative results. Hartree–Fock also optimizes the orbitals' shapes, density functional theory is often more accurate still, and post-Hartree–Fock methods improve on Hartree–Fock systematically, each at a greater computational cost.

concepts.name: Homonuclear diatomic molecule
concepts.statement: A molecule of two identical atoms, such as H₂, Li₂ or N₂.

concepts.name: Valence molecular orbitals
concepts.statement: When two atoms come close enough for their valence orbitals to overlap, the filled inner shells are largely unperturbed, so the molecular orbitals are built from the valence atomic orbitals alone.

concepts.name: Sigma orbitals from p orbitals
concepts.statement: Two np_z orbitals pointing at each other along the internuclear axis z combine head to head. Since their lobes alternate − + − + from left to right, their difference puts lobes of the same sign together and is the σ_np_z bonding orbital, and their sum, with a nodal plane between the atoms, the σ*_np_z antibonding one. An ns orbital on one atom and an np_z on the other combine the same way.

concepts.name: Pi orbital
concepts.statement: A molecular orbital formed from the side-to-side overlap of two parallel np_x (or np_y) orbitals. Their sum is the bonding π orbital, with more electron density above and below the internuclear axis; their difference is the antibonding π*, with a nodal plane perpendicular to the axis. π_np_x and π_np_y are a degenerate pair, and so are the two π*.

concepts.name: Rules for a molecular orbital diagram
concepts.statement: The number of molecular orbitals equals the number of atomic orbitals combined; the more two atomic orbitals overlap, the farther apart their bonding and antibonding combinations; a bonding orbital is stabilized about as much as its antibonding partner is destabilized; and orbitals interact most when their energies are the same. Head-on p_z overlap is greater than side-on, so σ and σ* are split more than π and π*.

concepts.name: Orbital order of the period 2 diatomics
concepts.statement: For O₂ and F₂ the valence orbitals run σ_2s < σ*_2s < σ_2p_z < π_2p < π*_2p < σ*_2p_z. For Li₂ through N₂ the interaction of the 2s orbital on one atom with the 2p_z on the other, strongest when their energies are close, pushes σ_2p_z above the π_2p pair; the 2s–2p gap grows with nuclear charge across the period.

concepts.name: Filling a molecular orbital diagram
concepts.statement: Count the valence electrons, place them in the molecular orbitals from the lowest energy up, two of opposite spin to an orbital (Pauli) and singly with parallel spins across a degenerate pair (Hund), then read off the electron configuration, the bond order and the number of unpaired electrons.

concepts.name: Bond order
concepts.statement: One-half the net number of bonding electrons, (bonding electrons − antibonding electrons)/2. It matches the number of electron pairs of a Lewis structure: 1, 2 and 3 for single, double and triple bonds.

forms.latex: \text{bond order} = \dfrac{\text{number of bonding electrons} - \text{number of antibonding electrons}}{2}

concepts.name: Bond order and bond strength
concepts.statement: A species whose bond order is greater than zero is predicted to be stable, and a higher bond order means a stronger, shorter bond: H₂⁺ and He₂⁺, with ½, have weaker and longer bonds than H₂, with 1. A bond order of 0 predicts no covalent bond.

concepts.name: Antibonding electrons outweigh bonding ones
concepts.statement: The antibonding σ*_1s orbital lies farther above the 1s energy than the bonding σ_1s lies below it, ΔE₋ > |ΔE₊|, so electrons in antibonding orbitals cancel and exceed the stabilization of as many electrons in bonding orbitals: equal numbers of each leave the molecule less stable than the separated atoms.

concepts.name: No covalent bond in He₂
concepts.statement: He₂'s four valence electrons fill both σ_1s and σ*_1s, (σ_1s)²(σ*_1s)², for a bond order of 0: molecular orbital theory predicts no stable covalent He₂.

concepts.name: Van der Waals helium dimer
concepts.statement: The van der Waals force, which also makes liquid helium possible, binds two helium atoms very weakly. Proposed by Slater in 1928 and observed in 1993, He₂ is the largest known ground-state molecule of two atoms, its wavefunction reaching far into the classically forbidden region beyond the shallow well.

concepts.name: Antisymmetric ground state of H₂
concepts.statement: The product |1σ¹α¹⟩|1σ²β²⟩ does not change sign when the electrons' labels are swapped; the combination (|1σ¹α¹1σ²β²⟩ − |1σ²α²1σ¹β¹⟩)/√2 does, p̂₁₂ψ = −ψ, and has the same energy, since the Hamiltonian holds no spin terms.

concepts.name: Properties of Slater determinants
concepts.statement: Exchanging two electrons changes a Slater determinant's sign, and two identical spin-orbitals make it zero, which is why an orbital holds one electron of each spin at most. In the independent-particle approximation its energy is the sum of its orbitals' energies; it is normalized when its orbitals are, and two determinants that differ in any one orbital are orthogonal.

concepts.name: Writing a molecule's Slater determinant
concepts.statement: Fill the molecular orbital diagram by the Aufbau and Pauli principles and write the N × N Slater determinant of the occupied spin-orbitals φ₁α, φ₁β, φ₂α, …, normalized by 1/√N!; the diagram then stands for that antisymmetrized wavefunction.

concepts.name: Paramagnetism
concepts.statement: A substance with unpaired electrons is paramagnetic: it is attracted into a magnetic field. Most substances have only paired electrons.

concepts.name: Paramagnetism of O₂
concepts.statement: Filling O₂'s 12 valence electrons leaves the last two in separate π*_2p orbitals with parallel spins: a bond order of 2 and a triplet with two unpaired electrons, so O₂ is paramagnetic, which is why liquid O₂ stays suspended between the poles of a magnet. Lewis and valence bond pictures cannot predict this.

concepts.name: Spin barrier
concepts.statement: Organic compounds, water, carbon dioxide and nitrogen have only paired electrons, while O₂ has two unpaired ones, so their reaction would need an electron of O₂ to change its spin. That costs a large input of energy, a spin barrier, which keeps organic matter from burning rapidly in air.

concepts.name: Heteronuclear diatomic molecule
concepts.statement: A diatomic molecule of two different atoms, such as NO, HCl or CN⁻.

concepts.name: Molecular orbitals of a heteronuclear diatomic
concepts.statement: When atom B is more electronegative than A, χ_B > χ_A, B's atomic orbitals lie lower, the diagram is skewed toward B and the bonding orbitals lie closer in energy to B's orbitals. The bonding electrons are then closer to B: molecular orbital theory's description of a polar covalent bond.

concepts.name: Nonbonding molecular orbital
concepts.statement: An orbital whose energy does not change when the molecule forms because it has no net overlap with the other atom's orbitals or too different an energy, such as chlorine's 3s, 3p_x and 3p_y in HCl. Filled, it is the molecular orbital equivalent of a lone pair, and its electrons do not count in the bond order.

concepts.name: Axial orbital angular momentum
concepts.statement: Λ, the projection of the electrons' orbital angular momentum on the internuclear axis, which plays the part of L in an atom: a state is Σ, Π, Δ, Φ for Λ = 0, 1, 2, 3.

concepts.name: Axial total angular momentum
concepts.statement: Ω, the projection of the total angular momentum, orbital and spin, on the internuclear axis.

concepts.name: Molecular term symbol
concepts.statement: The label ^{2S+1}Λ_{Ω,(g/u)}^{(+/−)} of an electronic state of a diatomic molecule: the spin multiplicity, the letter Σ, Π, Δ, Φ for Λ, the projection Ω of the total angular momentum, the parity g or u (homonuclear molecules only) and, for Σ states, the + or − symmetry to reflection in a plane containing the internuclear axis.

concepts.name: Finding the term symbols of a diatomic configuration
concepts.statement: Closed shells contribute ¹Σ⁺ and can be ignored. Combine the labels of the singly occupied orbitals with the allowed total spins: CO's excited configuration with one electron in a σ⁺ and one in a π orbital gives Π × Σ⁺ = Π, ¹Π and ³Π. Where two electrons share a degenerate π pair, list the microstates and read Λ, M_S, parity and reflection off them; O₂'s two π_g* electrons give ³Σ_g⁻, ¹Δ_g and ¹Σ_g⁺, with ³Σ_g⁻ the ground state.

concepts.name: Selection rules for diatomic molecules
concepts.statement: Electric dipole transitions between electronic states of a diatomic molecule obey ΔΛ = 0, ±1, ΔS = 0 and ΔΩ = 0, ±1, as atomic transitions obey their rules; Σ⁺ ↔ Σ⁻ is forbidden, and in a homonuclear molecule only g ↔ u.

concepts.name: Parity of a molecular state
concepts.statement: The parity of a state is the product of the parities of its open-shell electrons: g × g = g, g × u = u, u × u = g. Bonding σ and antibonding π orbitals are g; antibonding σ and bonding π are u.

concepts.name: Reflection symmetry of Σ states
concepts.statement: Reflection through a plane containing both nuclei leaves an orbital unchanged (+) or changes its sign (−), and a state's label is the product: (+)(+) = (−)(−) = +, (+)(−) = −. Of a degenerate π pair one orbital is + and the other −, and the label is written only for Σ states.

concepts.name: Valence bond theory
concepts.statement: One of the two basic quantum theories of the chemical bond, beside molecular orbital theory. It describes each bond as the pairing of an electron in an atomic orbital of one atom with an electron in an atomic orbital of the other, as a quantum version of the Lewis structure; lone pairs stay in the orbitals the bonds do not use. Molecular orbital theory instead spreads each orbital over the whole molecule.

concepts.name: Valence-bond wavefunctions of H₂
concepts.statement: Built from one 1s orbital on each proton, the two-electron function symmetric in the electrons' coordinates, ψ_g, is bonding and must carry the antisymmetric spin function; the antisymmetric one, ψ_u, carries the symmetric spin function and vanishes on the plane bisecting the bond, so it is antibonding. A single bond in F₂ (from 2p_z on each F) or in HF (H 1s with F 2p_z) takes the same gerade form.

concepts.name: Promotion of an electron
concepts.statement: To bond more often than its ground configuration allows, an atom is pictured as promoting an electron to a higher orbital (Be 1s²2s² to 1s²2s2p_z, C 1s²2s²2p² to 1s²2s2p³), making more unpaired electrons; the energy spent is repaid by the bonds formed.

concepts.name: Hybrid orbital
concepts.statement: A combination of the s and p orbitals of one atom, χ = C₁ψ_2s + C₂ψ_2px + C₃ψ_2py + C₄ψ_2pz, proposed by Pauling to give equivalent bonds where the atom's s and p orbitals are not. It solves the Schrödinger equation exactly only for hydrogen, where 2s and 2p have one energy; in a molecule the neighbours make 2s and 2p nearly degenerate.

concepts.name: Orthonormality of hybrid orbitals
concepts.statement: Hybrids of one atom are normalized and mutually orthogonal. For χ_i = a₁|2s⟩ + b₁|2p_z⟩ and χ_j = a₂|2s⟩ + b₂|2p_z⟩ the orthonormal atomic orbitals reduce this to a₁² + b₁² = 1, a₂² + b₂² = 1 and a₁a₂ + b₁b₂ = 0.

concepts.name: sp hybrid orbitals
concepts.statement: With equal s contributions the conditions give two sp hybrids, (ψ_2s ± ψ_2pz)/√2, pointing 180° apart: two equivalent orbitals for two equal bonds, as in linear BeH₂.

concepts.name: sp² hybrid orbitals
concepts.statement: One 2s and two 2p orbitals combine into three equivalent sp² hybrids in a plane, 120° apart, as in trigonal planar BH₃; the third p orbital is left over.

concepts.name: sp³ hybrid orbitals
concepts.statement: One 2s and three 2p orbitals combine into four equivalent sp³ hybrids, (1/2)(ψ_2s ± ψ_2px ± ψ_2py ± ψ_2pz) with an even number of minus signs among the p's, whose large lobes point to the corners of a tetrahedron, 109.5° apart, as in CH₄.

concepts.name: Hybridization is an interpretation
concepts.statement: A molecule does not take its shape because it is hybridized; the hybrids are a convenient reading of the wavefunction for the geometry the molecule has. Only the electron density is observable.

concepts.name: spˣ notation
concepts.statement: spˣ abbreviates a hybrid with s character 1/(x + 1) and p character x/(x + 1). x need not be an integer, and an atom's four orbitals may divide into hybrids of several kinds.

concepts.name: s and p character of a hybrid
concepts.statement: A hybrid |χ⟩ = N(p + γs), with γ the relative contribution of s, is normalized by N = 1/√(1 + γ²); its p character is 1/(1 + γ²) and its s character γ²/(1 + γ²).

concepts.name: Bond angle and hybrid composition
concepts.statement: Two equivalent hybrids N(p + γs) that are orthogonal point at an angle θ with cos θ = −γ²: an experimental bond angle fixes the hybrids' s character. 180° gives sp, 109.5° gives sp³.

concepts.name: Hybrids share out the s and p orbitals
concepts.statement: An atom's hybrids together hold all of its s and p orbitals: their p characters add up to 3 and their s characters to 1.

concepts.name: Hybrids of water
concepts.statement: Water's 104.5° angle gives γ = 0.5: each O–H bonding hybrid is 20% s and 80% p (nearer sp⁴ than sp³). The two lone-pair hybrids, assumed identical, then hold 30% s and 70% p and point about 115° apart, less directional and held closer to the O atom.

concepts.name: Canonical molecular orbitals
concepts.statement: Molecular orbitals that combine all the available atomic orbitals of a polyatomic molecule and spread over the whole molecule (delocalized), unlike the two-centre orbitals of valence bond theory.

concepts.name: Molecular orbitals of a linear AH₂ molecule
concepts.statement: The two H 1s orbitals and A's 2s, 2p_x, 2p_y, 2p_z make six molecular orbitals. In a linear molecule only 2s and 2p_z overlap the H orbitals: 2s with the in-phase H pair gives the bonding 2σ_g and an antibonding σ_g, 2p_z with the out-of-phase pair the bonding 1σ_u and an antibonding σ_u, and 2p_x, 2p_y stay nonbonding as the 1π_u pair.

concepts.name: Bonding in BeH₂
concepts.statement: The sum and difference of the two H 1s orbitals mix with Be's 2s and 2p_z; BeH₂'s four valence electrons fill the two bonding orbitals, so the molecule has two bonds and is linear, which atomic orbitals alone (two unpaired electrons at 90°) cannot explain.

concepts.name: Walsh diagram
concepts.statement: A plot of a molecule's calculated orbital energies against a change in its geometry, such as the H–A–H angle of an AH₂ molecule from 90° to 180°. It shows why related molecules with the same number of valence electrons share a shape.

concepts.name: HOMO and LUMO
concepts.statement: The highest occupied molecular orbital (HOMO) and the lowest unoccupied molecular orbital (LUMO), together called the frontier orbitals.

concepts.name: Walsh's rule
concepts.statement: A molecule adopts the structure that best stabilizes its HOMO; if a change of shape leaves the HOMO alone, the next occupied orbital decides. Read off a Walsh diagram it tells bent from linear, though not the exact angle.

concepts.name: Molecular orbitals of water
concepts.statement: In bent water, orbitals of the same symmetry (a₁, b₁, b₂) and comparable energy mix: 2a₁ from O 2s and the H σ combination, 1b₂ from O 2p_y and the H σ* combination, 3a₁ from O 2p_z and the H σ combination, and the HOMO 1b₁, the nonbonding O 2p_x. The two lone pairs therefore sit in different orbitals, not in two identical ones as valence bond theory has them.

concepts.name: Photoelectron spectroscopy
concepts.statement: Ionizing a sample with photons of one energy and measuring the kinetic energies of the emitted electrons. XPS uses soft X-rays (200–2000 eV) to reach core levels; UPS uses vacuum ultraviolet (10–45 eV) to reach valence levels, the molecular orbitals.

concepts.name: Vertical ionization energy
concepts.statement: The energy difference E(A⁺) − E(A) between the ion and the neutral with the ion formed at the neutral's geometry; the most probable transition, to the ion's vibrational level that best overlaps the neutral's v″ = 0. It is never smaller than the adiabatic ionization energy.

concepts.name: Adiabatic ionization energy
concepts.statement: The least energy that ionizes a molecule: from its ground vibrational state to the lowest vibrational level of the ion, in the ion's relaxed geometry.

concepts.name: Kinetic energy of a photoelectron
concepts.statement: Energy is conserved in A + photon → A⁺ + e⁻, and a free electron has only kinetic energy, so KE = hν − IE: Einstein's photoelectric equation with the ionization energy in place of the work function.

concepts.name: Photoelectron bands as orbital energies
concepts.statement: By Koopmans' theorem each band of a photoelectron spectrum stands for the removal of an electron from one occupied orbital, at an ionization energy close to minus that orbital's energy; orbitals bound more tightly than the photon energy do not appear.

concepts.name: Vibrational structure of a photoelectron band
concepts.statement: A band is split into peaks for the ion's vibrational levels. A long progression means the electron came from a bonding orbital whose loss changes the bond (H₂'s 1σ_g, N₂'s 1π_u, HCl's 3σ); a band with little structure comes from a nonbonding orbital (HCl's 1π).

concepts.name: Photoelectron spectrum of water
concepts.statement: Water's valence spectrum shows separate bands at 12.6 (1b₁), 14.7 (3a₁) and 18.5 eV (1b₂), with 2a₁ deeper at 32.2 eV, close to the Hartree–Fock orbital energies. Valence bond theory, with two identical bonds and two identical lone pairs, would give two bands; the spectrum supports the delocalized molecular orbitals.

concepts.name: Conjugated system
concepts.statement: A chain or ring of atoms whose aligned p orbitals overlap across the intervening single bonds, so that its π electrons are delocalized over the whole group rather than held in one bond.

concepts.name: Sigma–pi separability
concepts.statement: In a planar molecule the σ and π orbitals are orthogonal, so the σ-bonded framework (from sp² hybrids and H 1s) and the π framework (from the unhybridized 2p_z) can be treated independently: the π electrons move in the field of a σ framework already formed. Ethylene's two frameworks give separate σ and π orbitals.

concepts.name: Coulomb integral α
concepts.statement: In Hückel theory, the diagonal Hamiltonian matrix element H_ii = ⟨φ_i|Ĥ|φ_i⟩ of a carbon 2p_z orbital, set to the same α for every atom; negative.

concepts.name: Resonance integral β
concepts.statement: In Hückel theory, the off-diagonal matrix element H_ij between the 2p_z orbitals of two bonded atoms, set to the same β for every bonded pair and to zero otherwise. It is negative and sets the strength of the π bonding; a typical estimate is −75 kJ/mol.

concepts.name: Hückel approximation
concepts.statement: Only the π electrons of a planar conjugated molecule are treated, in orbitals built from one 2p_z per carbon, and the secular determinant is simplified by four assumptions: every overlap S_ij (i ≠ j) is zero, every Coulomb integral is α, the resonance integral is β between neighbours and zero between atoms not bonded. It is qualitative: electron repulsion is left out and energies are not accurate.

concepts.name: Hückel variable x
concepts.statement: The energy written as x = (α − E)/β, which turns the Hückel secular determinant into one with x on the diagonal; each root x gives an orbital energy E = α − xβ.

concepts.name: π orbitals of ethylene
concepts.statement: Ethylene's 2 × 2 Hückel determinant gives x² − 1 = 0, so E = α ± β: the bonding π₁ = (φ₁ + φ₂)/√2 at α + β and the antibonding π₂ = (φ₁ − φ₂)/√2, with one more node, at α − β. The two π electrons fill π₁.

concepts.name: HOMO–LUMO gap
concepts.statement: The energy difference between the highest occupied and the lowest unoccupied molecular orbitals.

concepts.name: Writing a Hückel determinant
concepts.statement: Dividing the Hückel secular determinant by β and writing x = (α − E)/β leaves the molecule's connection matrix: x on the diagonal, 1 for each pair of bonded atoms and 0 for each pair not bonded. Its roots in x give the orbital energies.

concepts.name: π orbitals of butadiene
concepts.statement: Butadiene's determinant expands to x⁴ − 3x² + 1 = 0, a quadratic in x², so x = ±0.618, ±1.618 and the energies are α ± 1.618β and α ± 0.618β. The orbitals' energies rise with their number of nodes, 0 to 3, as in a particle in a box; four π electrons give π₁²π₂².

concepts.name: Total π-electron energy
concepts.statement: The sum of the energies of the occupied π orbitals, each counted once for each electron in it.

concepts.name: Delocalization energy
concepts.statement: The extra stabilization of π electrons spread over the whole molecule: the total π energy minus that of the same number of isolated double bonds, each 2(α + β) as in ethylene. It is negative, since β is.

concepts.name: Delocalization energy of butadiene
concepts.statement: Butadiene's π energy 4α + 4.472β lies 0.472β below the 4α + 4β of two ethylene double bonds; with β ≈ −75 kJ/mol that is about −35 kJ/mol.

concepts.name: Resonance in valence bond theory
concepts.statement: Valence bond theory keeps two-centre bonds and describes a conjugated molecule as a superposition of resonance structures, weighted variationally; the minor structures' contribution gives a stabilization akin to the delocalization energy of molecular orbital theory.

concepts.name: Kekulé structures of benzene
concepts.statement: Kekulé's benzene is a ring of six carbons with alternating single and double bonds, written as two resonance structures. X-ray diffraction finds all six C–C bonds equal, 140 pm, between a double (135 pm) and a single bond (147 pm), so neither structure alone is right.

concepts.name: π orbitals of benzene
concepts.statement: Benzene's ring gives the cyclic Hückel determinant (1 also in the corners for the bond closing the ring), whose roots x = ±2, ±1, ±1 put the π levels at α + 2β, α + β (twice), α − β (twice) and α − 2β. The six π electrons fill the three bonding orbitals, π₁²π₂²π₃², for a total of 6α + 8β.

concepts.name: Delocalization energy of benzene
concepts.statement: Benzene's π energy lies 2β below that of three isolated double bonds, 6α + 6β; the thermochemical value is −152 kJ/mol. Heats of hydrogenation show it: benzene is about 150 kJ/mol more stable than a cyclohexatriene with three independent double bonds.

concepts.name: Hückel's rule
concepts.statement: A cyclic conjugated polyene is closed shell and especially stable, aromatic, when it has 4n + 2 π electrons (n = 0, 1, 2 …: 2, 6, 10 …). These molecules have the largest delocalization energies.

concepts.name: Ab initio calculation
concepts.statement: A calculation of a molecule's electronic structure from the postulates of quantum mechanics alone, with no empirical parameters or experimental data; semi-empirical methods do use them. For a closed-shell molecule it uses the electronic Hamiltonian with a single Slater determinant built from molecular orbitals, each a linear combination of contracted Gaussian basis functions whose coefficients the self-consistent field and linear variational methods choose to minimize the energy.

concepts.name: Molecular orbitals in a basis set
concepts.statement: Each molecular orbital of an ab initio calculation is a linear combination of the basis functions, ψ_j = Σ_k c_jk φ_k; the coefficients c_jk are the variational parameters, and the number of basis functions fixes the number of molecular orbitals and the size of the matrices to be solved.

concepts.name: Hartree–Fock limit
concepts.statement: As the basis set is enlarged, the variational energy of a single-determinant wavefunction falls toward a limit it cannot pass: the Hartree–Fock limit. The energy there is the Hartree–Fock energy, its orbitals the Hartree–Fock orbitals and its determinant the Hartree–Fock wavefunction.

concepts.name: Restricted and unrestricted Hartree–Fock
concepts.statement: In a restricted Hartree–Fock calculation, electrons of α and β spin are constrained to the same spatial orbitals; an unrestricted calculation lets each spin have its own spatial orbitals. Unrestricted orbitals can describe the electrons better, especially in a molecule with an odd number of electrons, but need twice as many spatial orbitals.

concepts.name: Molecular orbitals of carbon monoxide
concepts.statement: Huo's 1965 ab initio calculation of CO in a basis of the ten 1s, 2s and 2p orbitals of C and O gives, in order of energy, the oxygen and carbon 1s cores (1σ, 2σ), a bonding 3σ, an antibonding 4σ, two degenerate bonding π orbitals and a nonbonding 5σ, an sp hybrid pointing away from oxygen on carbon. Donation of the 5σ electrons explains why CO binds iron through carbon, and the hybrid mixing of 2s and 2p comes out of the calculation without being put in.

concepts.name: Cartesian Gaussian-type orbital
concepts.statement: A Gaussian-type orbital written in Cartesian coordinates, N e^{−αr²}(x − x₀)^a (y − y₀)^b (z − z₀)^c, centred at (x₀, y₀, z₀); α sets its width, and the nonnegative integers a, b, c, with a + b + c = ℓ, choose its shape as ℓ and m do for an atomic orbital.

concepts.name: Cartesian against spherical Gaussians
concepts.statement: For angular momentum ℓ there are (ℓ + 1)(ℓ + 2)/2 Cartesian Gaussians but only 2ℓ + 1 spherical-harmonic ones; from ℓ = 2 on the Cartesian set holds extra functions of lower ℓ (x² + y² + z² is an s function among the six d's), which a transformation removes, leaving 5 d functions rather than 6.

concepts.name: Gaussians miss the nuclear cusp
concepts.statement: A Gaussian e^{−αr²} is flat at the nucleus and falls off too fast far away, where a Slater-type orbital e^{−ζr} has a cusp at r = 0 and a slower exponential tail; no single Gaussian has the right shape near or far from the nucleus.

concepts.name: Gaussian integrals are cheap
concepts.statement: Integrals over Gaussian functions are far cheaper than over Slater-type orbitals: every overlap integral has a closed form, and most Coulomb and exchange integrals split into products of one-dimensional ones (about 600 evaluations against 100⁶ for a six-dimensional integral on a 100-point grid). So even though several Gaussians are needed for each Slater function, Gaussian calculations reach the same accuracy in much less time.

concepts.name: Primitive Gaussian
concepts.statement: A single Gaussian-type function with its own fixed exponent α and coefficient d, the building block of a contracted Gaussian function.

concepts.name: Contracted Gaussian function
concepts.statement: A fixed linear combination of primitive Gaussians treated as one basis function: its coefficients and exponents are set beforehand, usually to imitate a Slater-type orbital, and are not varied in the energy calculation. A basis function built this way is called a contraction.

concepts.name: STO-NG basis set
concepts.statement: The minimal basis set in which each Slater-type orbital is replaced by a contraction of N primitive Gaussians whose coefficients d_in and exponents α_in maximize the overlap with that Slater orbital; once fitted, each contraction acts as a single atomic orbital.

concepts.name: Fitting a Slater orbital with Gaussians
concepts.statement: Choosing the coefficients and exponents of a few Gaussians so that their sum follows a Slater-type orbital, and judging the fit by plotting the two together: the sum can match the middle of the orbital closely but stays flat at the nucleus and falls too fast in the tail.

concepts.name: Pople basis set notation
concepts.statement: The names of Pople's Gaussian basis sets, N-MPG: N primitives for each inner-shell orbital, a hyphen for a split (double-zeta) valence shell whose inner and outer functions are built from M and P primitives, and G for Gaussian; a star adds polarization functions and a plus diffuse functions.

concepts.name: Minimal basis set
concepts.statement: The smallest basis that holds every occupied orbital of each atom and the whole of any partly filled shell (all three 2p orbitals of carbon), with the p shell added for the alkali and alkaline earth metals: one 1s function for each hydrogen, 1s, 2s and three 2p for carbon.

concepts.name: Orbital function
concepts.statement: A basis function in the role an atomic orbital plays in an LCAO calculation: the Hamiltonian matrix has one row per orbital function, and only their weights are varied. Each may be built from several Gaussian primitives, whose exponents and coefficients stay fixed.

concepts.name: Contraction notation
concepts.statement: A basis set's contraction is written (primitives) → [orbital function shells]: carbon in STO-3G is (6s3p) → [2s1p], six s-type primitives contracted into two s functions and three p-type primitives into one p shell, five orbital functions in all. In a segmented contraction each primitive belongs to one orbital function; in a general contraction a primitive may appear in several.

concepts.name: Single-zeta basis set
concepts.statement: A basis that represents each atomic orbital by one orbital function: one value of ζ for a Slater orbital, or one contraction of Gaussians imitating it. Every minimal basis is single zeta.

concepts.name: Multiple-zeta basis set
concepts.statement: A basis that represents each atomic orbital by several orbital functions with different ζ, two in a double-zeta (DZ) and three in a triple-zeta (TZ) basis; the variational weights then mix compact and diffuse functions, so each atom's orbitals can change their radial shape in the molecule.

concepts.name: Flexibility of a basis set
concepts.statement: The variety of shapes a basis lets the wavefunction take around each nucleus. More functions per atomic orbital give more flexibility and a better reproduction of the molecular wavefunction, as the hydrogen in HF needs a different 1s shape from the hydrogen in H₂, but the functions lose their meaning as atomic orbitals and must be optimized directly in atomic calculations.

concepts.name: Cost of a larger basis
concepts.statement: A calculation's cost grows steeply with the number of orbital functions: doubling them from N to 2N makes the Hamiltonian a 2N × 2N matrix with, even using its Hermiticity, about 3 to 4 times as many matrix elements to evaluate.

concepts.name: Split-valence basis set
concepts.statement: A basis with a single orbital function for each core orbital and several for each valence orbital, putting flexibility where bonding distorts the electron density and saving it near the nuclei, where the core electrons change little.

concepts.name: Pople split-valence basis sets
concepts.statement: Pople's split-valence sets X-YG: a contraction of X primitives for each core orbital and one orbital function per digit of Y for each valence orbital, each digit giving its primitives. In 3-21G the core orbitals are 3-primitive contractions and each valence orbital has a 2-primitive, compact function and a 1-primitive, diffuse one. Their exponents and coefficients are optimized in Hartree–Fock calculations on the atoms.

concepts.name: Polarization function
concepts.statement: An orbital function with a higher ℓ than the atom's valence orbitals (p on hydrogen, d on carbon), added so that the electron density can shift and bend away from the nucleus as a bond makes its surroundings anisotropic. In Pople's names one star adds them to the heavier atoms and two stars to hydrogen and helium as well, each from a single Gaussian primitive.

concepts.name: Diffuse function
concepts.statement: A broad orbital function with a very small exponent, added to describe electron density far from the nuclei, as in anions, excited states and weakly bound complexes. In Pople's names one plus adds a single-primitive s and p set to each atom heavier than helium, two pluses an s function to hydrogen and helium too.

concepts.name: Choosing a basis set
concepts.statement: The accuracy of a calculation rests on a basis flexible enough to fit the true wavefunction, but every added function costs time, and heavier atoms need more functions; the choice of basis is a trade between the two.

concepts.name: Effective core potential
concepts.statement: A potential added to the Hamiltonian in place of many of an atom's core electrons, which cuts the number of integrals for heavy atoms; it fails for properties sensitive to the wavefunction near the nucleus, such as X-ray spectra and NMR shielding.

concepts.name: Symmetry simplifies quantum calculations
concepts.statement: The symmetry of a molecule can show, rigorously and without computing them, that many of the Hamiltonian matrix elements and overlap integrals of a secular determinant are zero, so qualitative information about molecular orbitals, rotations and vibrations comes without the full calculation. Group theory is the mathematics of that symmetry.

concepts.name: A change of basis leaves the roots unchanged
concepts.statement: Any basis spanning the same space can represent the secular determinant; a linear combination of the original basis functions changes the matrix but not its roots, as a curve is the same in Cartesian or polar coordinates. Benzene's Hückel determinant has the roots ±2, ±1, ±1 in either basis.

concepts.name: A block-diagonal determinant factors
concepts.statement: In a basis of suitable linear combinations the secular determinant takes a block-diagonal form, which expands into the product of the smaller determinants of its blocks; benzene's 6 × 6 determinant becomes two 1 × 1 and two 2 × 2 blocks.

concepts.name: Symmetry operation
concepts.statement: An action that leaves an object looking the same after it has been carried out: a permutation of the atoms that leaves the molecule indistinguishable from its starting state, every point moving to an equivalent position.

concepts.name: Symmetry element
concepts.statement: The point, line (axis) or plane with respect to which a symmetry operation is carried out: all the points that stay in the same place when the operation is performed.

concepts.name: Identity
concepts.statement: The operation E of doing nothing, whose symmetry element is the whole molecule; every molecule has it.

concepts.name: n-fold rotation
concepts.statement: The operation C_n rotates the object counterclockwise about an axis by 2π/n (360°/n); n successive C_n return it to the start, and C_n^m is written in lowest terms.

concepts.name: Principal axis
concepts.statement: Of a molecule's rotation axes, the one with the highest n; by convention the z axis lies along it.

concepts.name: Reflection
concepts.statement: The operation σ reflects the object in a mirror plane. A plane containing the principal axis is vertical, σ_v; one perpendicular to it is horizontal, σ_h; a vertical plane bisecting two C₂ axes is dihedral, σ_d. Two reflections in the same plane are the identity.

concepts.name: Inversion
concepts.statement: The operation i passes every point through the centre of symmetry to the same distance on the other side; a molecule has at most one inversion centre, and two inversions are the identity.

concepts.name: Improper rotation
concepts.statement: The rotation-reflection S_n: a rotation C_n about an axis followed by a reflection in the plane perpendicular to it. S₁ is a reflection and S₂ an inversion; S_n^n = E for even n, while for odd n S_n^n = σ and S_n^{2n} = E.

concepts.name: Proper and improper operations
concepts.statement: The identity and rotations can actually be carried out on a molecule and are proper symmetry operations; reflections, inversions and improper rotations can only be imagined and are improper.

concepts.name: Axes of a molecule
concepts.statement: The convention for Cartesian axes on a molecule: the origin at the central atom or centre, z along the principal axis, x in the molecular plane (or the plane holding the most atoms), y completing a right-handed set.

concepts.name: Point group
concepts.statement: The complete collection of symmetry elements a molecule possesses, which classifies it; at least one point stays unchanged under every operation. Chemists name them in Schönflies notation (C₂ᵥ, D₆ₕ, T_d …), crystallographers in Hermann–Mauguin notation.

concepts.name: Families of point groups
concepts.statement: The common point groups fall into nonrotational groups (C₁, C_i, C_s), single-axis groups (C_n, C_nv, C_nh, S_n), dihedral groups with n C₂ axes perpendicular to the principal axis (D_n, D_nd, D_nh, D_∞h) and cubic groups with several high-order axes (T, T_d, T_h, O, O_h, I_h).

concepts.name: Assigning a point group
concepts.statement: Finding a molecule's point group by asking, in the flowchart's order, whether it is linear, has several high-order axes, a C_n axis, perpendicular C₂ axes, a σ_h, vertical or dihedral planes, or an S_2n axis.

concepts.name: Which molecules can be polar
concepts.statement: A dipole moment must lie along every C_n axis and cannot be reversed by any operation, so only molecules of the groups C_n, C_nv and C_s can be polar, with the dipole along the axis in C_n and C_nv.

concepts.name: Which molecules can be chiral
concepts.statement: A molecule is chiral, not superimposable on its mirror image, exactly when it has no improper rotation axis S_n; a centre of inversion or any mirror plane rules chirality out.

concepts.name: Group
concepts.statement: A set of elements with a rule for combining them that obeys four criteria: it contains the identity, it is closed (every product is an element), the combination is associative, and every element has an inverse in the set. A molecule's symmetry operations, combined by applying one after another, form a group.

concepts.name: Order of a group
concepts.statement: The number of elements h of a group.

concepts.name: Abelian group
concepts.statement: A group whose elements all commute, g_ig_k = g_kg_i; group elements need not commute, and a group whose do not is non-Abelian (C₃ᵥ: σ_vC₃ ≠ C₃σ_v).

concepts.name: Class
concepts.statement: Symmetry operations related to each other by other operations of the group belong to the same class: in NH₃ the three mirror planes form one class and C₃⁺ and C₃⁻ another.

concepts.name: Group multiplication table
concepts.statement: A table of the products of every pair of a group's operations, the operation along the top applied first and the one at the side second; every row and column holds every operation once.

concepts.name: Matrix representation
concepts.statement: A set of transformation matrices Γ(g), one representative for each symmetry operation g, acting on a chosen basis (unit vectors, atomic orbitals); the representatives multiply as the operations do and obey every condition of a group. The basis is said to span the representation.

concepts.name: Matrices of the symmetry operations
concepts.statement: On the vector (x, y, z) the identity is the unit matrix, a reflection changes the sign of the coordinate normal to its plane, inversion changes all three, and C_n about z is the rotation matrix through 2π/n.

concepts.name: Reducible representation
concepts.statement: A matrix representation in a basis such as NH₃'s four valence s orbitals, whose matrices can be reduced to the irreducible representations of the character table; different bases are chosen to extract different properties.

concepts.name: Similarity transform
concepts.statement: The representatives of an operation in two bases related by a matrix of coefficients C are related by a similarity transform.

concepts.name: Character
concepts.statement: The trace χ(g) of a matrix representative Γ(g). It is unchanged by a similarity transform, and operations of one class have the same character in a given representation.

concepts.name: Character table
concepts.statement: The table of a point group's irreducible representations (rows) against its classes of operations (columns), with the characters in the body, the order h, and the functions (x, y, z, R_x, R_y, R_z and their products) that transform as each representation.

concepts.name: Characters by inspection
concepts.statement: Finding a character without the matrix: for each basis function add 1 if the operation leaves it unchanged, −1 if it changes its sign and 0 if it moves; an axis rotated through θ contributes cos θ.

concepts.name: Irreducible representation
concepts.statement: One of the limited number of ways a function can transform under a group's operations, its symmetry species; functions transforming alike form bases for the same representation and are said to have the same symmetry. Labels: A or B (nondegenerate, symmetric or antisymmetric under the principal rotation), E and T (doubly and triply degenerate), Σ, Π, Δ in infinite groups, with g/u, primes and subscripts 1, 2 for further symmetry.

concepts.name: Complex characters come in pairs
concepts.statement: Where characters are complex, in powers of ε = exp(2πi/n), the irreducible representations come in conjugate pairs; chemists add each pair into one real representation (C₃'s E: 2, −1, −1).

concepts.name: Correlation of a group with a subgroup
concepts.statement: When a molecule's symmetry descends to a subgroup, each irreducible representation of the group correlates with one or a sum of the subgroup's (a degenerate E or T may split); correlation diagrams and tables show these relations, and an infinite group is reduced through a finite subgroup (C₂ᵥ for C_∞v, D₂ₕ for D_∞h).

concepts.name: Direct product of representations
concepts.statement: The representation whose characters are the products of the characters of its factors at each operation; its dimension is the product of theirs. It may be reducible, and it contains the totally symmetric representation only when a representation is multiplied by itself.

concepts.name: When an integral must vanish
concepts.statement: An integral is a number and is invariant to every symmetry operation, so it can be non-zero only if its integrand transforms as, or contains, the totally symmetric irreducible representation; group theory identifies integrals that are necessarily zero.

concepts.name: Homogeneous equations need a zero determinant
concepts.statement: A set of simultaneous linear equations Ax = b has a unique solution only when det A ≠ 0; homogeneous equations (b = 0), such as the secular equations, have a non-trivial solution only when det A = 0, and any multiple of a solution is one, so the orbitals can be normalized.

concepts.name: Reduction formula
concepts.statement: The number of times the kth irreducible representation appears in a representation: the sum over classes of the class size times the two characters, divided by the order of the group.

concepts.name: Building molecular orbitals with symmetry
concepts.statement: Choose a basis of valence orbitals, find the irreducible representations it spans, build the SALCs of each, combine those of the same species into molecular orbitals, write and solve the secular determinant, back-substitute for the coefficients and normalize.

concepts.name: Energies from a 2 × 2 secular determinant
concepts.statement: With normalized functions (S₁₁ = S₂₂ = 1) the 2 × 2 secular determinant is a quadratic in E whose two roots are the orbital energies; where H₁₂ = S₁₂ = 0 the roots are H₁₁ and H₂₂ themselves.

concepts.name: Ammonia's orbitals from s SALCs
concepts.statement: NH₃'s valence s basis spans 2A₁ + E: the two A₁ SALCs, s_N and (s₁ + s₂ + s₃)/√3, mix into a bonding and an antibonding orbital, while the two E SALCs do not mix (H₃₄ = S₃₄ = 0) and form a degenerate pair.

concepts.name: Degrees of freedom
concepts.statement: The number of independent ways a molecule can move; each atom has three, along x, y and z, so a molecule of N atoms has 3N.

concepts.name: The 3N Cartesian basis
concepts.statement: A set of x, y, z axes on each of a molecule's N atoms, the basis for its motions; its character under an operation is the character of (x, y, z) times the number of atoms the operation leaves unshifted.

concepts.name: Symmetries of the vibrations
concepts.statement: Subtracting the translations (the characters of x, y, z) and the rotations (of R_x, R_y, R_z) from the 3N Cartesian characters leaves the representation of the vibrations, which reduces to their symmetries: H₂O vibrates as 2A₁ + B₁.

concepts.name: Reducing a representation by table
concepts.statement: Reducing a representation by a table: for each irreducible representation multiply class size, its character and the reducible character, sum each row and divide by h. NH₃'s motions give Γ = 3A₁ + A₂ + 4E, and Γ_vib = 2A₁ + 2E once A₁ + E (translations) and A₂ + E (rotations) are taken off.

concepts.name: Normal modes of a molecule
concepts.statement: The vibrations of a polyatomic molecule, each a concerted motion of groups of bonds (stretching, bending, torsion) that transforms as one irreducible representation of the molecule's point group.

concepts.name: Number of vibrational modes
concepts.statement: Three of a molecule's 3N degrees of freedom are translations and three rotations (two for a linear molecule, whose spin about its axis moves no atom), leaving 3N − 6 vibrational modes for a nonlinear molecule and 3N − 5 for a linear one.

concepts.name: Selection rules from symmetry
concepts.statement: A transition is allowed by symmetry only if the direct product of the symmetries of the initial state, the transition operator and the final state contains the totally symmetric irreducible representation.

concepts.name: Which vibrations are IR active
concepts.statement: A vibration that changes the dipole moment absorbs infrared light: light polarized along x, y or z excites vibrations of the same symmetry as x, y or z in the character table (in H₂O, z-polarized light the A₁ modes and x-polarized the B₁ stretch).

concepts.name: Raman scattering
concepts.statement: A two-photon process: a photon lifts the molecule to a short-lived virtual state, not an eigenstate of the molecule, which emits a photon and leaves it in a different vibrational state.

concepts.name: Which vibrations are Raman active
concepts.statement: Since two photons of possibly different polarizations take part, a Raman transition transforms as a Cartesian product (x², xy, yz …); a vibration of the same symmetry as one of them is Raman active.

concepts.name: Polarizability
concepts.statement: The constant (in fact a tensor) α relating the dipole a field induces to the field.

concepts.name: Symmetry-adapted linear combination
concepts.statement: A linear combination of basis functions (bond stretching vectors or atomic orbitals) that transforms as one irreducible representation; SALCs show the symmetries of stretches and, built from atomic orbitals, the LCAO molecular orbitals.

concepts.name: Projection operator
concepts.statement: Applying each operation of the group to one basis function, weighting the image by the character of an irreducible representation and summing gives a SALC of that symmetry, or zero where the basis does not span it.

concepts.name: Normalizing a SALC
concepts.statement: Multiplying a SALC by one over the square root of the sum of the squares of its coefficients.

concepts.name: SALCs of bond stretches
concepts.statement: The stretching vectors of a molecule combine into SALCs whose symmetries are those of its stretching modes: water's two O–H stretches give a symmetric A₁ and an antisymmetric combination, (b₁ ± b₂)/√2; para- and ortho-difluorobenzene's C–H stretches give different sets.

concepts.name: Only orbitals of one symmetry bond
concepts.statement: The overlap of two atomic orbitals transforms as the direct product of their symmetries and is non-zero only if it contains the totally symmetric representation, so two orbitals can bond only if they belong to the same symmetry species.

concepts.name: Molecular orbitals from SALCs
concepts.statement: A molecular orbital is a linear combination of the SALCs of one symmetry species; group theory gives its form but not the coefficients or energies, which the secular equations do. Water's valence basis spans 3A₁ + 2B₁ + B₂.

concepts.name: Symmetry of an electronic state
concepts.statement: The symmetry of an electronic state is the direct product of the symmetries of the orbitals holding unpaired electrons; a closed-shell ground state is totally symmetric.

concepts.name: Which electronic transitions light can drive
concepts.statement: Light polarized along x, y or z transforms as x, y or z, so from a totally symmetric ground state it reaches only excited states of that symmetry: NH₃'s x, y light reaches E states and z light A₁; H₂O's (1B₂)¹(2B₁)¹ state, of A₂ symmetry, cannot be reached by one photon.

concepts.name: Electromagnetic radiation
