concepts.statement: Θ_vib is higher the stronger the bond and the lighter the (effective) mass of the molecule; molecules with low Θ_vib often dissociate at lower temperatures.

concepts.name: Molar heat capacity at constant volume
concepts.statement: The heat capacity at constant volume of one mole, C̄_V = (∂E/∂T)_V with E the molar energy.

concepts.name: Temperature derivative in terms of β
concepts.statement: Since β = 1/kT, a derivative in T is a derivative in β times ∂β/∂T: ∂/∂T = −(1/kT²)∂/∂β = −kβ²∂/∂β.

concepts.name: Vibrational heat capacity of a diatomic
concepts.statement: A diatomic's vibration contributes k(Θ_vib/T)² e^(−Θ_vib/T)/(1 − e^(−Θ_vib/T))² per molecule to the heat capacity, R per mole at high T and zero at low T; it depends on T only through T/Θ_vib.

concepts.name: Vibrational populations
concepts.statement: The fraction of molecules in vibrational state v is f_v = (1 − e^(−Θ_vib/T))e^(−vΘ_vib/T).

concepts.name: Most molecules are in the ground vibrational state
concepts.statement: At room temperature most molecules are in the ground vibrational state v = 0; only molecules with very weak bonds and low vibrational temperatures populate excited vibrational states significantly.

concepts.name: Rotational partition function
concepts.statement: The sum over a diatomic's rotational levels of the Boltzmann factor times the degeneracy 2J + 1, q_rot = Σ(2J + 1)e^(−E_J/kT).

concepts.name: Rotational temperature
concepts.statement: The characteristic temperature Θ_rot = ħ²/2Ik = hcB̃/k, about the temperature at which kT is comparable to the spacing of the rotational levels and excited rotational levels become important.

concepts.name: When the rotational sum becomes an integral
concepts.statement: Replacing the rotational sum by an integral needs T ≫ Θ_rot; only the lightest gases at cryogenic temperatures need the discrete sum, while vibrations at room temperature are in the discrete limit.

concepts.name: Rotational heat capacity of a diatomic
concepts.statement: The rotational energy of N diatomic molecules is NkT, so rotation contributes R to the molar heat capacity of a diatomic.

concepts.name: Heat capacity as a sum of contributions
concepts.statement: The heat capacity of a molecular gas breaks down into translational, rotational, vibrational (and electronic) contributions, C = C_trans + C_vib + C_rot.

concepts.name: Heat capacities of monatomic and diatomic gases
concepts.statement: With the vibrational and electronic contributions negligible at room temperature, C_v = (3/2)nR for a monatomic gas and (3/2)nR + nR = (5/2)nR for a diatomic.

concepts.name: Most molecules are rotationally excited
concepts.statement: Rotational energies are less than vibrational and electronic energies, so at room temperature many rotational states are populated.

concepts.name: Symmetry number
concepts.statement: The number σ of distinct ways a molecule can be brought into identical configurations by rotations; a homonuclear diatomic has σ = 2, a heteronuclear one σ = 1.

concepts.name: Rotational partition function at high temperature
concepts.statement: When the rotational levels lie close together the sum becomes an integral, q_rot = kT/B̃; dividing by the symmetry number to correct the overcounting of a homonuclear molecule's states gives q_rot = kT/σB̃ = T/σΘ_rot.

concepts.name: Vibrational partition function of a polyatomic molecule
concepts.statement: The normal modes are independent oscillators, so the vibrational partition function is the product over the modes, q_vib = Π e^(−Θ_vib,i/2T)/(1 − e^(−Θ_vib,i/T)).

concepts.name: Vibrational energy of a polyatomic gas
concepts.statement: The vibrational energy of N molecules is a sum over the modes, ⟨E_vib⟩ = Nk Σ[Θ_vib,i/2 + Θ_vib,i e^(−Θ_vib,i/T)/(1 − e^(−Θ_vib,i/T))].

concepts.name: Vibrational heat capacity of a polyatomic gas
concepts.statement: Each normal mode adds its own oscillator term to the heat capacity, C̄_V = Nk Σ(Θ_vib,i/T)² e^(−Θ_vib,i/T)/(1 − e^(−Θ_vib,i/T))².

concepts.name: Vibrational entropy and conformations
concepts.statement: The vibrational energy and entropy depend on the shape of the potential energy surface, so the vibrational entropy computed from the normal modes shows whether entropy favours one conformation of a molecule over another.

concepts.name: Center of mass
concepts.statement: The point about which the mass-weighted coordinates of the atoms sum to zero, Σm_ix_i = Σm_iy_i = Σm_iz_i = 0.

concepts.name: Rotational partition function of a spherical top
concepts.statement: With levels J(J + 1)ħ²/2I of degeneracy (2J + 1)² and T ≫ Θ_rot, the sum becomes an integral and q_rot = (π^{1/2}/σ)(T/Θ_rot)^{3/2}.

concepts.name: Rotational partition function of a symmetric top
concepts.statement: Converting the sum over J and K to an integral gives q_rot = (√π/σ)(8π²I_BkT/h²)(8π²I_AkT/h²)^{1/2}.

concepts.name: Rotational partition function of an asymmetric top
concepts.statement: Integrating classically over the three angular momenta and the orientations and dividing by σh³ gives q_rot = (√π/σ)√(T³/Θ_AΘ_BΘ_C), with a characteristic rotational temperature Θ = h²/8π²Ik for each principal axis.

forms.latex: q_{rot} = \dfrac{\pi^2}{\sigma} \sqrt{\dfrac{8 \pi I_A kT}{h^2}} \sqrt{\dfrac{8 \pi I_B kT}{h^2}} \sqrt{\dfrac{8 \pi I_C kT}{h^2}}

concepts.name: Rotational energy of a nonlinear molecule
concepts.statement: In the classical approximation the molar rotational energy of a nonlinear molecule is (3/2)RT and its rotational heat capacity (3/2)R.

concepts.name: Specific heat capacity
concepts.statement: The heat C_s required to raise the temperature of one gram of a substance by one kelvin.

concepts.name: Molar heat capacity from the specific heat
concepts.statement: The product of the specific heat capacity and the molar mass is the molar heat capacity; for metals Dulong and Petit's law makes it about 25 J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹.

concepts.name: Atomic weights from Dulong and Petit's law
concepts.statement: Measuring a metal's specific heat capacity and dividing 3R by it gave its atomic weight, a simpler method than the disputed gravimetric ones of the time.

concepts.name: Constant-pressure and constant-volume heat capacities of solids
concepts.statement: Tabulated heat capacities are measured at constant pressure, but for simple solids C_p and C_v are essentially equal.

concepts.name: Ortho hydrogen
concepts.statement: Hydrogen whose two nuclear spins are parallel, the three triplet nuclear spin states.

concepts.name: Para hydrogen
concepts.statement: Hydrogen whose two nuclear spins are antiparallel, the singlet nuclear spin state.

concepts.name: Exchange symmetry of the nuclei of H₂
concepts.statement: The protons are spin-½ fermions, so H₂'s total wavefunction is antisymmetric under their exchange; translation, vibration and the electrons do not change sign, so the product of the nuclear spin and rotational wavefunctions must be antisymmetric.

concepts.name: Exchange parity of the rotational wavefunctions
concepts.statement: Exchanging the nuclei takes θ to π − θ and φ to φ + π, which multiplies the rotational wavefunction by (−1)^J: it is symmetric for even J and antisymmetric for odd J.

concepts.name: Ortho and para partition functions
concepts.statement: Para hydrogen (the singlet) takes the even rotational levels and ortho hydrogen (the triplet, weight 3) the odd ones: q_ortho = 3Σ_odd(2J + 1)e^(−J(J+1)Θ_R/T), q_para = Σ_even(2J + 1)e^(−J(J+1)Θ_R/T).

concepts.name: Ortho to para ratio
concepts.statement: At equilibrium N_o/N_p = 3Σ_odd(2J + 1)e^(−J(J+1)Θ_R/T) / Σ_even(2J + 1)e^(−J(J+1)Θ_R/T), which tends to 3 at high temperature and to 0 as T → 0.

forms.latex: \frac{N_{o}}{N_{p}}=\frac{3 \sum_{J=1,3,5, \ldots}(2 J+1) e^{-J(J+1) \Theta_{R} / T}}{\sum_{J=0,2,4,\ldots} (2 J+1) e^{-J(J+1) \Theta_{R} / T}}

concepts.name: Frozen high-temperature ortho–para mixture
concepts.statement: Ortho–para interconversion is very slow without a catalyst such as activated charcoal, so hydrogen cooled from high temperature keeps its 3:1 ratio and its rotational heat capacity is ¾ that of ortho plus ¼ that of para.

concepts.name: Rotational states of oxygen-16
concepts.statement: The nuclei of ¹⁶O₂ have zero spin and are bosons, so only one parity of rotational state is allowed and only every other rotational level contributes to its partition function.

concepts.name: Equipartition theorem
concepts.statement: Every degree of freedom that appears only quadratically in the total energy has an average energy of ½k_BT in thermal equilibrium and contributes ½k_B to the heat capacity.

concepts.name: Average translational energy
concepts.statement: From the translational partition function, ⟨E_trans⟩ = −(1/q_trans)∂q_trans/∂β = (3/2)k_BT: each of the three translational degrees of freedom provides ½k_BT.

concepts.name: Average rotational energy of a diatomic
concepts.statement: From the rotational partition function, ⟨E_rot⟩ = k_BT: a diatomic's two rotational degrees of freedom each provide ½k_BT.

concepts.name: Average vibrational energy
concepts.statement: From the vibrational partition function, ⟨E_vib⟩ = hcν̃/(e^(hcν̃/k_BT) − 1), which tends to k_BT when hcν̃ ≪ k_BT, one ½k_BT for each of the oscillator's two quadratic terms.

concepts.name: Frozen-out degree of freedom
concepts.statement: A degree of freedom whose quantum level spacing is not small beside k_BT; its heat capacity is reduced and drops to zero at low temperature, as for vibrations at room temperature.

concepts.name: Heat capacity by equipartition
concepts.statement: Each quadratic term contributes ½R to the molar heat capacity: translation (3/2)R, rotation R for a linear and (3/2)R for a nonlinear molecule, and R for each vibrational mode that is not frozen out.

concepts.name: Heat capacity of a diatomic gas against temperature
concepts.statement: The molar heat capacity of a diatomic gas rises from (3/2)R through (5/2)R to (7/2)R as rotation and then vibration stop being frozen out, near T_rot and T_vib respectively.

concepts.name: Fundamental equation for the internal energy
concepts.statement: For a reversible change with only PV work, the first law with δq_rev = TdS and δw_rev = −PdV gives dU = TdS − PdV, an exact differential since U, S and V are all state functions; for an irreversible change dU ≤ TdS − PdV.

concepts.name: Natural variables of the internal energy
concepts.statement: The variables in which dU = TdS − PdV expresses U, so U = U(S, V): S and V are the natural variables of U.

concepts.name: Entropy change with temperature at constant volume
concepts.statement: At constant volume dU = TdS and C_V = (∂U/∂T)_V, so dS = (C_V/T)dT and ΔS = ∫C_V(T)/T dT from T₁ to T₂.

concepts.name: Entropy increases with temperature
concepts.statement: Since a heat capacity is always positive, entropy must increase as the temperature increases.

concepts.name: Fundamental equation for the enthalpy
concepts.statement: From H = U + PV and dU = TdS − PdV, a reversible change gives dH = TdS + VdP: the natural variables of H are S and P.

concepts.name: Entropy change with temperature at constant pressure
concepts.statement: At constant pressure dH = TdS and C_P = (∂H/∂T)_P, so dS = (C_P/T)dT and ΔS = ∫C_P(T)/T dT; this is the more common route, since heat capacities are easier to measure at constant pressure.

concepts.name: Absolute entropy
concepts.statement: The entropy measured from a natural zero, S(0) = 0 for a perfect crystal at 0 K, so that S(T) follows from heat-capacity data alone; unlike the enthalpy, which has only a floating zero point.

concepts.name: Third law of thermodynamics
concepts.statement: The entropy of a pure substance in a perfect crystalline form approaches zero as T approaches zero (but perfect crystals do not exist).

concepts.name: A perfect crystal at 0 K has one microstate
concepts.statement: A perfect crystal at 0 K has only one arrangement of its lowest energy, W = 1, so S = k ln W = 0; above 0 K more microstates are accessible and S > 0.

concepts.name: Entropy of fusion
concepts.statement: Ice and water in equilibrium melt reversibly at one temperature, so Δ_fus S = q_rev/T = Δ_fus H/T, and the entropy curve jumps by this amount at the melting point.

concepts.name: Standard molar entropy
concepts.statement: The absolute entropy of one mole of a substance in its standard state (1 bar), S°, found from calorimetric data and tabulated against temperature.

concepts.name: Heavier particles have more entropy
concepts.statement: The particle-in-a-box energies have the mass in the denominator, so the levels crowd together as m increases: more levels within reach, more entropy, as the noble gases show.

concepts.name: Residual entropy
concepts.statement: The nonzero entropy a real crystal keeps as T approaches 0 K, because it is frozen into more than one ground-state arrangement; an exception to the third law, which assumes a perfect crystal with a single ground state.

concepts.name: Entropy of orientational disorder
concepts.statement: If each of N molecules can sit in the lattice in two orientations, W = 2^N and S = k ln 2^N = Nk ln 2, 5.7 J/(mol K) per mole, as for solid CO.

concepts.name: Entropy of a phase transition
concepts.statement: A phase transition at equilibrium at constant T and P has Δ_trs G = Δ_trs H − T_trs Δ_trs S = 0, so Δ_trs S = Δ_trs H/T_trs.

concepts.name: Temperature derivative of the Gibbs energy
concepts.statement: At constant pressure the temperature derivative of the molar Gibbs energy is minus the molar entropy.

concepts.name: First-order transition
concepts.statement: A phase transition in which a first derivative of G (or A), such as S, jumps at the transition temperature.

concepts.name: Heat capacity at a first-order transition
concepts.statement: A second derivative of G, such as the heat capacity, displays a singularity (+∞) at a first-order transition point.

concepts.name: Kinds of phase transition
concepts.statement: Vaporization (l → g), condensation (g → l), fusion (s → l), freezing (l → s), sublimation (s → g), deposition (g → s) and solid-to-solid transitions; each has a change in entropy.

concepts.name: Debye model of a crystal
concepts.statement: Debye treated the vibrations of a crystal lattice as a collection of quantized normal modes, phonons; at low temperature only the low-frequency modes are accessible, so the heat capacity falls sharply, and at high temperature it approaches the classical Dulong–Petit limit.

concepts.name: Debye T³ law
concepts.statement: At low temperature the heat capacity of a nonmetallic crystal is proportional to T³, C_P = aT³.

concepts.name: Low-temperature heat capacity of a metal
concepts.statement: In a metal the conduction electrons add a term linear in T to the lattice's T³ term, C_P = aT + bT³.

concepts.name: Absolute entropy from calorimetry
concepts.statement: With S(0) = 0 from the third law, the absolute entropy at T is the integral of C_p/T from 0 K plus ΔH_trs/T_trs for every phase transition on the way: S(T) = ∫₀ᵀ C_p/T dT + Σ ΔH_trs/T_trs.

concepts.name: Finding an absolute entropy along a heating path
concepts.statement: Split the warming from 0 K into stretches of one phase, integrate C_P/T over each with that phase's heat capacity, and add ΔH_trs/T_trs at each transition, as for CO₂ gas at 300 K through its sublimation at 194.7 K.

concepts.name: Entropy from the partition function near absolute zero
concepts.statement: As T goes to zero only the n degenerate ground states contribute to Q = Σ e^(−E_j/kT), so S = k_B ln Q + k_BT(∂ln Q/∂T) approaches k_B ln n, which is zero for a nondegenerate ground state, consistent with the third law.

concepts.name: More complex molecules have more entropy
concepts.statement: A molecule with more atoms, or a nonlinear one, has more rotational and vibrational modes to take up energy, so more accessible microstates and a higher standard molar entropy.

concepts.name: Spectroscopic entropy
concepts.statement: The standard entropy of a gas calculated from spectroscopic data through its partition function, S°_calc, as against the calorimetric S°_exp.

concepts.name: Residual entropy from spectroscopic and calorimetric entropies
concepts.statement: Where a substance can exist in many configurations at 0 K (glass, ice, carbon monoxide), its calorimetric entropy falls short of the spectroscopic one, and the residual entropy is the difference S̄_calc − S̄_exp.

concepts.name: Standard entropy of a reaction
concepts.statement: Because entropy is a state function, the standard entropy change of a reaction is the sum of the standard entropies of the products less that of the reactants, each times its stoichiometric coefficient.

concepts.name: Natural variables
concepts.statement: The variables in which a state function's fundamental equation writes it: S and V for U, S and P for H, V and T for A, P and T for G. They are the convenient variables to describe the function.

concepts.name: Helmholtz energy
concepts.statement: The state function A ≡ U − TS, also called the Helmholtz free energy.

concepts.name: Helmholtz energy decreases in a spontaneous change at constant T and V
concepts.statement: At constant temperature and volume dA = dU − TdS ≤ 0: A decreases in a spontaneous change, whether or not the system is isolated, and is constant once equilibrium is reached.

concepts.name: Helmholtz energy as the maximum work
concepts.statement: At constant temperature ΔA = ΔU − q_rev = w_rev, the maximal work a system can produce; at constant volume this is work other than volume work.

concepts.name: Helmholtz energy of mixing two ideal gases
concepts.statement: Mixing two ideal gases at constant temperature and total volume has ΔU = 0, so ΔA_molar = RT(y₁ ln y₁ + y₂ ln y₂), which is negative because the mole fractions are below one.

concepts.name: Fundamental equation for A
concepts.statement: dA = −PdV − SdT, so the natural variables of A are V and T.

concepts.name: Gibbs energy
concepts.statement: The state function G ≡ H − TS = U + PV − TS = A + PV, the counterpart of A for changes at constant pressure.

concepts.name: Gibbs energy decreases in a spontaneous change at constant T and P
concepts.statement: At constant temperature and pressure dG ≤ 0, and between two states ΔG = ΔH − TΔS ≤ 0: G decreases in a spontaneous change and is constant at equilibrium (ΔG = 0); a process with ΔG > 0 does not occur spontaneously.

concepts.name: Driving a process by coupling
concepts.statement: A process with positive ΔG can be made to occur only when it is coupled with a process that has a negative ΔG.

concepts.name: Temperature can reverse the spontaneous direction
concepts.statement: Because the entropy term of ΔG = ΔH − TΔS carries T, the spontaneous direction of a process can change with temperature: NH₃(g) + HCl(g) → NH₄Cl(s), with ΔH = −176.2 kJ and ΔS = −0.285 kJ/K, is spontaneous at 298 K and runs in reverse above 618 K.

concepts.name: Gibbs energy as the maximum non-PV work
concepts.statement: At constant T and P, dG = δw_rev − δw_volume: ΔG is the maximal reversible, isobaric, isothermal work other than PV work that a spontaneous change can perform.

concepts.name: Fundamental equation for G
concepts.statement: dG = VdP − SdT, so the natural variables of G are P and T, those of most laboratory experiments.

concepts.name: First derivatives of U
concepts.statement: Comparing dU = TdS − pdV with the total differential of U(S, V) gives (∂U/∂S)_V = T and (∂U/∂V)_S = −p.

concepts.name: Euler relation for an exact differential
concepts.statement: For an exact differential the two mixed second partial derivatives are equal: differentiating the coefficient of one variable by the other gives the same result either way round.

concepts.name: Maxwell relations
concepts.statement: Equalities between partial derivatives of T, S, p and V that follow from the Euler relation applied to dU, dH, dA and dG; they let a convenient derivative, perhaps one in α and κ_T, stand in for an inconvenient one.

concepts.name: First derivatives of H
concepts.statement: (∂H/∂S)_p = T and (∂H/∂p)_S = V; so (∂U/∂S)_V = (∂H/∂S)_p, both equal to T.

concepts.name: Thermal expansion coefficient
concepts.statement: α = (1/V)(∂V/∂T)_p, the fractional change of volume with temperature at constant pressure.

concepts.name: Isothermal compressibility
concepts.statement: κ_T = −(1/V)(∂V/∂p)_T, the fractional decrease of volume with pressure at constant temperature; it is small for solids.

concepts.name: Thermodynamic equation of state
concepts.statement: (∂U/∂V)_T = T(∂p/∂T)_V − p = Tα/κ_T − p, from dU = TdS − pdV and the Maxwell relation from A (Example 22.3.1).

concepts.name: First derivatives of G
concepts.statement: (∂G/∂T)_P = −S and (∂G/∂P)_T = V: entropy and volume are first-order derivatives of G.

concepts.name: Pressure dependence of the enthalpy
concepts.statement: (∂H/∂P)_T = V − T(∂V/∂T)_P, from G = H − TS, (∂G/∂P)_T = V and the Maxwell relation from G.

concepts.name: Enthalpy of an ideal gas is independent of pressure
concepts.statement: For an ideal gas (∂V/∂T)_P = nR/P, so (∂H/∂P)_T = V − T(nR/P) = 0: H does not depend on P.

concepts.name: The fundamental thermodynamic equations
concepts.statement: The four differentials dU = TdS − pdV, dH = TdS + Vdp, dG = VdP − SdT and dA = −pdV − SdT write U, H, G and A in their natural variables; they assume only PV work and reversible processes, and are essentially equations of state from which experimental data give G or H.

concepts.name: Chemical potential
concepts.statement: μ_i, the chemical potential of species i: the coefficient of dn_i in the fundamental equations once the amounts of the species may change.

concepts.name: Fundamental equations with changing composition
concepts.statement: When the amounts may change, each fundamental equation gains Σμ_i dn_i: dU = TdS − PdV + Σμ_i dn_i, dH = TdS + VdP + Σμ_i dn_i, dG = −SdT + VdP + Σμ_i dn_i, dA = −SdT − PdV + Σμ_i dn_i.

concepts.name: First derivatives of A
concepts.statement: (∂A/∂V)_T = −P and (∂A/∂T)_V = −S: pressure and entropy are first-order derivatives of A.

concepts.name: Standard state of a gas
concepts.statement: A pure ideal gas at 1 bar, the standard state conditions (SSC) in which data are tabulated, marked with °; the temperature is stated with the data and is not part of the definition.

concepts.name: Gibbs energy of an ideal gas against pressure
concepts.statement: For a mole of ideal gas ΔG_molar = RT ln(P₂/P₁), and with P₁ the standard state of 1 bar, G_molar(P) = G°_molar + RT ln(P/1 bar).

concepts.name: Gibbs energy of a solid against pressure
concepts.statement: A solid's volume hardly changes with pressure, so G(P_final) ≈ G(P_initial) + VΔP.

concepts.name: Gibbs–Helmholtz equation
concepts.statement: (∂(G/T)/∂T)_P = −H/T², and for a process (∂(ΔG/T)/∂T)_P = −ΔH/T²: H is a first-order derivative of G/T.

concepts.name: Gibbs energy as a function of temperature
concepts.statement: G(T) = H(T) − TS(T) is continuous at phase transitions, where Δ_trs H = T_trs Δ_trs S, and descends with temperature; its slope −S jumps at each transition, so the curve has kinks at the melting and boiling points. It is plotted as G(T) − H(0).

concepts.name: Fugacity
concepts.statement: The property f that Lewis defined in 1905 by dḠ = RT d ln f, extending the ideal-gas expression dḠ = RT d ln P to every substance; for an ideal gas f = P.

concepts.name: Fugacity coefficient
concepts.statement: φ = f/P, unity for a gas that behaves ideally, so it measures non-ideality: the closer φ is to one, the closer the gas is to the ideal state.

concepts.name: Fugacity approaches pressure as P → 0
concepts.statement: In the zero-pressure limit every gas behaves ideally, so dḠ → RT d ln P and f → P.

concepts.name: Fugacity of a component of a mixture
concepts.statement: dḠ_i = RT d ln f_i, where Ḡ_i and f_i are the partial molar Gibbs energy and fugacity of the i-th component; in terms of the chemical potential, dμ̄_i = RT d ln f_i.

concepts.name: Chemical potential from the fugacity
concepts.statement: Integrating dμ̄ = RT d ln f from the standard state gives μ̄ = μ̄° + RT ln(f/P°).

concepts.name: Heat
concepts.statement: Energy that flows into or out of a system as heat, q; in the absence of other changes it would change the system's temperature.

concepts.name: Work
concepts.statement: Energy that flows as work, w: an infinitesimal displacement of the system multiplied by the force that resists it, integrated along the path the change follows.

concepts.name: Change in internal energy
concepts.statement: The change in internal energy between the initial and final states of a system, ΔU = U_f − U_i.

concepts.name: First law of thermodynamics
concepts.statement: The capacity of a system to do work is increased by heating the system or doing work on it: the change in its internal energy is the heat that flows in plus the work done on it, ΔU = q + w.

concepts.name: Endothermic and exothermic processes
concepts.statement: A process in which heat flows into the system is endothermic (q_system > 0); one in which heat flows out of the system is exothermic (q_system < 0).

concepts.name: Heat capacity
concepts.statement: The heat needed per unit rise in temperature, C = dq/dT, so that dq = C dT; it is usually given per mole, in J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹.

concepts.name: State function
concepts.statement: A property of a system whose value depends only on the system's state, so that its change between two states is the same whatever path joins them; U and p are state variables.

concepts.name: Partial derivative
concepts.statement: The slope of a function of several variables with respect to one of them while the others are held fixed.

forms.latex: \left( \dfrac{ \partial f}{\partial x_i} \right)_{x_j \neq i} = \lim_{\Delta _i \rightarrow 0} \left( \dfrac{f(x_1+ \Delta x_1 , x_2 + \Delta x_2, \dots, x_i +\Delta x_i, \dots x_n+\Delta x_n) - f(x_1,x_2, \dots x_i, \dots x_n) }{\Delta x_i} \right)

concepts.name: Total differential
concepts.statement: An infinitesimal change in a function of several variables is the sum of its partial derivatives, each times the change in its own variable, so each contribution can be considered separately; for an ideal gas dp = (∂p/∂V)_T dV + (∂p/∂T)_V dT.

forms.latex: dp = \left( \dfrac{\partial p}{ \partial V} \right)_{T} dV + \left( \dfrac{\partial p}{ \partial T} \right)_{V} dT

concepts.name: Pressure is a state function
concepts.statement: The change in pressure of an ideal gas between two states comes out the same whether it goes by an isothermal step then an isochoric one or the other way round: pressure is a state variable, and its change does not depend on the pathway.

concepts.name: Kinds of work
concepts.statement: Work can be expansion against a resisting pressure, pushing charge through a circuit, extension against a tension or stretching a surface against a surface tension; each is an infinitesimal displacement times a resisting force.

concepts.name: Work as a line integral
concepts.statement: Work is the integral along the path of the inner product of a force and the path element, w = ∫F·ds.

concepts.name: Sign convention for heat and work
concepts.statement: Positive heat and positive work are energy put into the system; energy the system gives off as heat or work takes a minus sign.

concepts.name: External pressure
concepts.statement: The pressure the surroundings exert on the system, P_ext, as on the outside of a piston.

concepts.name: Pressure-volume work
concepts.statement: The work of a change of volume against a pressure, w_PV = −∫P dV in the sign convention; one form of work among others.

concepts.name: Work against a constant external pressure
concepts.statement: When the external pressure is constant, the work is w = −P_ext ΔV; if it changes along the way, w = −∫P_ext(V) dV.

concepts.name: Irreversible process
concepts.statement: A process in which the system's pressure differs from the pressure exerted on it, so the system passes through states out of equilibrium that cannot be drawn on a PV diagram; the forces balance only at the end.

concepts.name: Work as an area on a PV diagram
concepts.statement: The work of a volume change is the area under the external pressure on a PV diagram between the initial and final volumes, even where the process itself cannot be drawn.

concepts.name: Path function
concepts.statement: A quantity, such as work or heat, that depends on the path taken between two states; it is an energy transfer, not a property of the system.

concepts.name: Reversible process
concepts.statement: A path that follows a series of states at rest, the forces balanced at all times (P_ext = P), as in a compression in infinitesimally small steps.

concepts.name: Work of a reversible isothermal volume change
concepts.statement: For an ideal gas changed reversibly at constant temperature from V₁ to V₂, w = −nRT ln(V₂/V₁).

concepts.name: Reversible paths need least work and deliver most
concepts.statement: Between the same two states, the reversible isothermal path needs the least work to compress a gas and gets the most work out of its expansion; a one-step irreversible path needs more and delivers less.

concepts.name: Exact and inexact differentials
concepts.statement: A straight d marks the change of a state function (dU), a crooked δ the path-dependent amounts of heat and work (δq, δw); only ΔU = U₂ − U₁ follows from the end points alone.

concepts.name: Internal energy is a state function
concepts.statement: The internal energy is conserved: around any closed cycle its change is zero, ∮dU = 0, though heat and work can be produced, destroyed and turned into each other.

concepts.name: Isothermal change of an ideal gas leaves U unchanged
concepts.statement: The energy of an ideal gas depends only on its temperature, so in an isothermal change ΔU = 0 and the work and the heat cancel, w = −q.

concepts.name: Heat of a reversible isothermal expansion
concepts.statement: In a reversible isothermal expansion of an ideal gas the heat taken in is q_rev = nRT ln(V₂/V₁), positive when V₂ > V₁.

concepts.name: Adiabatic process
concepts.statement: A process in which no energy as heat crosses the system's boundary, δq = 0.

concepts.name: In an adiabatic process the energy change is the work
concepts.statement: With no heat flowing, dU = δw_rev: the work of an adiabatic expansion comes from the internal energy, so the temperature of the gas drops.

concepts.name: Energy change of an ideal gas from its heat capacity
concepts.statement: Since the energy of an ideal gas changes only with temperature, dU = C_V dT along any path; per mole dŪ = C̄_V dT.

concepts.name: Two reversible paths between the same states
concepts.statement: Going from P₁, V₁, T₁ to P₂, V₂, T₁ along the isotherm A or along the adiabat B and the isochore C gives the same ΔU = 0, but the heats and works differ: w_B = −q_C and w_A ≠ w_B, so work is a path function even when reversible.

forms.latex: \Delta U_{B+C} = \Delta U_A = 0 = q_B + w_B + q_C + w_C

concepts.name: Heat capacities of an ideal gas at constant pressure and volume
concepts.statement: For an ideal gas the molar heat capacities differ by the gas constant, C̄_P − C̄_V = R; for n moles C_p = C_V + nR.

concepts.name: Heat capacity ratio
concepts.statement: The ratio γ = C̄_P/C̄_V of the constant-pressure and constant-volume heat capacities; for an ideal gas R/C̄_V = γ − 1.

concepts.name: Temperature and volume in a reversible adiabatic change
concepts.statement: Along a reversible adiabatic path of an ideal gas, T₂/T₁ = (V̄₁/V̄₂)^(γ−1): as the volume increases the temperature decreases.

concepts.name: Molecular interpretation of heat and work
concepts.statement: A change in the energy of a system, dU = Σ ε_j dN_j + Σ N_j dε_j, has two parts: heat shifts the populations of fixed energy levels, and reversible work shifts the levels themselves while the populations stay put; the pressure follows from the partition function as P = kT(∂ln Q/∂V).

concepts.name: Enthalpy
concepts.statement: The state function H ≡ U + PV.

concepts.name: Differential of the enthalpy
concepts.statement: Under reversible conditions with no work other than pressure-volume work, dH = δq + V dP.

concepts.name: Heat at constant pressure is the enthalpy change
concepts.statement: With no other work, the heat taken in at constant pressure is the enthalpy change, ΔH = q_P, as the heat at constant volume is the energy change, ΔU = q_V.

concepts.name: Molar heat of fusion
concepts.statement: The heat needed at constant pressure to melt one mole of a solid, Δ_fus H = H_liquid − H_solid at the melting point.

concepts.name: Enthalpy and energy differ for gases
concepts.statement: Because the volume change is small, U ≈ H for condensed matter; the difference matters for gases.

concepts.name: Heat capacity is a path function
concepts.statement: The heat capacity depends on what is kept constant: at constant volume and at constant pressure it differs, little for most materials and by nR for an ideal gas.

concepts.name: Heat capacity at constant pressure
concepts.statement: The rate of change of the enthalpy with temperature at constant pressure, C_P = (∂H/∂T)_P.

concepts.name: Finding enthalpies from heat capacities
concepts.statement: Measuring C_p as a function of temperature and integrating it gives H(T), relative to a reference temperature, with the heat of each phase transition added where H jumps.

concepts.name: Heat capacity at a phase transition
concepts.statement: At a phase transition H jumps at a fixed temperature, so ΔH/ΔT is infinitely large and C_p has a singularity.

concepts.name: There are no absolute enthalpies
concepts.statement: Only differences in enthalpy, ΔH, are properly defined, and only for processes.

concepts.name: Adding enthalpy changes along a process
concepts.statement: Define the process, then add the enthalpy change of each step: heating each phase (∫C_P dT) and each transition, as ΔH_total = ΔH₁ + Δ_fus H + ΔH₃ for warming ice from −20 to +20 °C.

concepts.name: Differential scanning calorimetry
concepts.statement: Heating a sample pan and an empty reference pan at a constant rate, the small temperature difference between them measures the heat capacity of the sample against temperature; a melting shows as a broadened peak whose area is Δ_fus H.

concepts.name: Reaction enthalpy
concepts.statement: The enthalpy change Δ_rH of a reaction as written: doubling the equation doubles it, and the reverse reaction has the same enthalpy with the opposite sign.

concepts.name: Hess's law
concepts.statement: Because enthalpy is a state function, enthalpy changes of reactions are additive: the enthalpy of a reaction that is the sum of steps is the sum of their enthalpies, so it can be found even when the reaction is hard to carry out.

concepts.name: Standard state
concepts.statement: The most stable form of a substance at 1 atmosphere pressure and the specified temperature.

concepts.name: Standard formation reaction
concepts.statement: The reaction that forms one mole of a substance in its standard state from its elements in their standard states.

concepts.name: Standard enthalpy of formation
concepts.statement: The enthalpy of a standard formation reaction, ΔH_f°; for a pure element in its standard state it is zero, which sets the zero of the enthalpy scale.

concepts.name: Reaction enthalpy from enthalpies of formation
concepts.statement: A reaction enthalpy is the sum of the enthalpies of formation of the products less that of the reactants, each times its stoichiometric coefficient.

concepts.name: Electron affinity
concepts.statement: The first electron affinity is −ΔH(0 K) of X(g) + e⁻ → X⁻(g), defined with a minus sign so that most are positive; later electron affinities add further electrons.

concepts.name: Average bond enthalpy
concepts.statement: The enthalpy D(X–Y) of breaking a bond in the gas, XY(g) → X(g) + Y(g), averaged over many molecules that contain that bond.

concepts.name: Estimating a reaction enthalpy from bond enthalpies
concepts.statement: In the absence of formation enthalpies, ΔH_rxn ≈ Σ(bonds broken) − Σ(bonds formed), reliable to within about 5–10% since the bond enthalpies are averages for the gas phase.

concepts.name: Kirchhoff's law
concepts.statement: At constant pressure the enthalpy change over a temperature change is the integral of the heat capacity, ΔH = ∫C_p dT, which is C_pΔT when C_p is constant; for a reaction, ΔH_rxn(T₂) = ΔH_rxn(T₁) + ∫ΔC_p dT.

concepts.name: Empirical heat capacity model
concepts.statement: A common empirical fit of heat capacities over broad temperature ranges, C_p(T) = a + bT + c/T², with a, b and c found by experiment.

concepts.name: Enthalpy change from the empirical heat capacity
concepts.statement: Integrating a + bT + c/T² gives ΔH = a(T₂ − T₁) + (b/2)(T₂² − T₁²) − c(1/T₂ − 1/T₁).

concepts.name: Spontaneous process
concepts.statement: A process that happens of its own accord once it is allowed to, such as a gas filling an evacuated chamber or two gases mixing when a valve is opened.

concepts.name: Energy does not decide spontaneity
concepts.statement: The state functions U and H give no clue which way a process goes: KNO₃ dissolves spontaneously and the solution gets cold, KOH dissolves spontaneously and it gets hot, so the first law is not enough to describe nature.

concepts.name: Number of distinguishable arrangements
concepts.statement: n distinguishable objects can be arranged in n! ways; when they fall in groups of a, b, c … indistinguishable objects, the count is n!/(a!b!c!…), the number of realizations W.

concepts.name: Expansion of an ideal gas into a vacuum
concepts.statement: A model experiment in which nothing happens but a spontaneous expansion and a change in entropy: no energy change, no heat, no work, no interactions.

concepts.name: Expansion adds ways to share the same energy
concepts.statement: When the box grows its energy levels crowd together, so the same average energy ⟨E⟩ can be realized in more ways; Boltzmann put the number of ways the energy can be distributed, not the energy itself, at the root of entropy.

concepts.name: Boltzmann's entropy formula
concepts.statement: Entropy is the logarithm of the number of realizations W, the number of ways the same energy can be distributed in the ensemble, times Boltzmann's constant; the logarithm makes entropies add when the W of two ensembles multiply, and a perfectly ordered ensemble, W = 1, has S = 0.

concepts.name: Entropies add as numbers of realizations multiply
concepts.statement: Two ensembles together have W_tot = W₁W₂ arrangements, while their entropies should add; a logarithm turns the product into the sum.

concepts.name: More accessible states drive expansion and mixing
concepts.statement: Expanding into a vacuum or mixing gives the molecules more energy states to use, which raises W and so S, and that is why the process is spontaneous.

concepts.name: Energy dispersal
concepts.statement: In an isolated system a spontaneous process balances lowering the energy against spreading it out; at constant energy the system evolves to maximize the dispersal of its energy.

concepts.name: Reversible heat is not a state function
concepts.statement: For an ideal gas δq_rev = C_v dT + P dV, and ∂C_v/∂V = 0 while ∂P/∂T = nR/V, so δq_rev is not an exact differential.

concepts.name: 1/T as an integrating factor
concepts.statement: Multiplying δq_rev by 1/T gives δq_rev/T = (C_v/T)dT + (P/T)dV, whose cross derivatives both vanish, so the result is exact.

concepts.name: Entropy
concepts.statement: The state function whose differential is the reversible heat divided by the temperature; it measures the dispersal of energy, or equivalently the number of possible microstates of a system.

concepts.name: A state function integrates to zero around a cycle
concepts.statement: Because U, H and S are state functions, each integrates to zero over any circular path that returns to the initial conditions.

concepts.name: Entropy change of an isothermal expansion
concepts.statement: For n moles of ideal gas taken from V₁ to V₂ at constant temperature, ΔS = q_rev/T = nR ln(V₂/V₁).

concepts.name: Entropy change on heating at constant volume
concepts.statement: Heating reversibly at constant volume changes the entropy by the integral of C_v/T over the temperature.

concepts.name: Entropy is a state function
concepts.statement: Along the isotherm A and along the adiabat B with the isochore C the reversible heats differ, but the entropy changes are the same, nR ln(V₂/V₁): entropy is a state function while q_rev is not.

concepts.name: Isolated system
concepts.statement: A system from which nothing gets in or out, neither heat nor mass nor radiation; a little universe all to itself, more than merely adiabatic.

concepts.name: Entropy produced by heat flowing between two bodies
concepts.statement: When two blocks at different temperatures exchange energy in isolation, dS = dU_A(1/T_A − 1/T_B), which is positive while the temperatures differ and zero when they are equal.

concepts.name: Entropy change of two identical blocks reaching one temperature
concepts.statement: Two identical blocks of heat capacity C_V at T_A and T_B reach the average temperature, and the entropy rises by C_V ln[(T_A + T_B)²/4T_AT_B], always positive.

concepts.name: Second law of thermodynamics
concepts.statement: The entropy of an isolated system never decreases; a spontaneous process in an isolated system produces entropy, dS > 0, which is a criterion for spontaneity.

concepts.name: Entropy production and exchange
concepts.statement: A system's entropy change splits into entropy produced inside it and entropy exchanged with the surroundings along with heat; a reversible change produces none, an isolated system exchanges none.

concepts.name: Clausius inequality
concepts.statement: Generalizing the isolated, irreversible and reversible cases, a system's entropy change is at least the heat it exchanges divided by the temperature.

concepts.name: Microstates as the measure of energy dispersal
concepts.statement: The number W of microstates available in a macrostate can be taken as the quantitative measure of energy dispersal; the more chaotic a system, the greater the dispersal and the entropy.

concepts.name: Calculating an entropy change along a reversible path
concepts.statement: Find ΔS of any process, an irreversible one included, by devising a reversible path between the same two states and integrating δq_rev/T along it.

concepts.name: Entropy change of the surroundings
concepts.statement: In a reversible isothermal expansion the surroundings give up the heat the system takes in at the same temperature, so ΔS_surr = −nR ln(V₂/V₁); in an expansion into a vacuum they exchange nothing and ΔS_surr = 0.

concepts.name: Total entropy change of a process
concepts.statement: ΔS_total = ΔS_sys + ΔS_surr is zero for the reversible isothermal expansion and nR ln(V₂/V₁) > 0 for the expansion into a vacuum between the same states.

concepts.name: Mole fraction
concepts.statement: The amount of one component divided by the total amount, χ_A = n_A/n_tot.

concepts.name: Entropy of mixing
concepts.statement: Ideal gases at the same pressure that mix each expand into the total volume, and the molar entropy rises by −R Σ χ_i ln χ_i; it is the main reason gases, and solutions, diffuse and mix.

concepts.name: Dissipation
concepts.statement: The conversion of work into heat, which the second law does not limit; heat into work is limited.

concepts.name: Heat engine
concepts.statement: A device that runs a working substance around a cycle, taking heat from a hot source, doing work and passing the rest of the heat to a cold sink.

concepts.name: Carnot cycle
concepts.statement: The reversible cycle of an ideal gas through an isothermal expansion at T_h, an adiabatic cooling to T_c, an isothermal compression at T_c and an adiabatic heating back to T_h.

concepts.name: The work of a cycle is the area it encloses
concepts.statement: The work a cycle produces is the area under the upper curve minus that under the lower one, the area enclosed on the PV diagram; it vanishes when T_h = T_c.

concepts.name: Efficiency of a heat engine
concepts.statement: The work the engine delivers per heat it takes in at the hot temperature.

concepts.name: Carnot efficiency
concepts.statement: A reversible engine between T_h and T_c has efficiency 1 − T_c/T_h, which reaches 1 only if T_c = 0 K and is zero when T_c = T_h; heat dissipated isothermally cannot be retrieved as work.

concepts.name: Heat pump
concepts.statement: A heat engine run backwards: work put in moves heat from cold to hot, so the warm side receives the work plus the heat pumped from the cold side; a refrigerator is one.

concepts.name: Stirling cycle
concepts.statement: The reversible cycle of an ideal gas through two isotherms, at T_h and T_c, joined by two isochores, whose heats cancel.

concepts.name: Entropy from the probabilities of the states
concepts.statement: With Stirling's approximation and a_j = p_jA, Boltzmann's S = k ln W of the ensemble divided by the number of systems gives S = −k Σ p_j ln p_j; a system certain to be in one state has zero entropy.

concepts.name: Entropy from the partition function
concepts.statement: Putting the Boltzmann probabilities p_j = e^{−βE_j}/Q into S = −k Σ p_j ln p_j gives S = U/T + k ln Q.

concepts.name: Statistical and thermodynamic entropy agree
concepts.statement: Differentiating S = −k_B Σ p_j ln p_j, with Σ dp_j = 0 and Σ ln p_j dp_j = −δq_rev/k_BT, gives dS = δq_rev/T: the statistical definition explains why the thermodynamic one works.

concepts.name: Kinds of equilibrium
concepts.statement: On a curve of G against one variable, a stable equilibrium is the absolute minimum, a metastable one a higher local minimum and an indifferent one a flat stretch where the second derivative is zero too; a labile equilibrium is a maximum that any small deviation leaves; every other point is unstable, since dG is not zero there and a spontaneous process can take place.

concepts.name: Fluctuations of the Gibbs energy
concepts.statement: The Boltzmann distribution is only the most likely one, so slightly less likely distributions with a little less entropy and a slightly higher G occur from time to time: G and its variables fluctuate about an equilibrium, little in a large system and relatively more in a small one, and the slope of G drives them back to a stable or metastable minimum.

concepts.name: Critical opalescence
concepts.statement: Where G is indifferent in the density, as near a critical point, the density fluctuates strongly; the refractive index follows it and the fluid scatters light strongly and turns milky.

concepts.name: Phase diagram
concepts.statement: A unary phase diagram maps the equilibrium states of a single pure substance in the P–T plane: regions where one phase is stable, separated by the curves where two coexist; usually only stable equilibria are drawn, metastable ones sometimes dashed.

concepts.name: Equilibrium vapor pressure
concepts.statement: The pressure at which the G(P) curve of the vapor crosses that of the liquid (or solid): below it the vapor is stable, above it the condensed phase, and only at it do both coexist. Plotted against T it gives the vaporization (or sublimation) curve.

concepts.name: Coexistence curves
concepts.statement: The three curves of a unary phase diagram: the liquid–vapor curve of equilibrium vapor pressures, the gas–solid (sublimation) curve, and the nearly vertical liquid–solid (melting) curve, which leans forward for most substances and backward for water, which expands on freezing.

concepts.name: Boiling
concepts.statement: A liquid boils when its equilibrium vapor pressure equals the total pressure over it, so that evaporation is no longer limited to the surface; in a sealed container the pressure rises with temperature and boiling may never be reached.

concepts.name: Triple point
concepts.statement: The one point where the three coexistence curves meet and solid, liquid and vapor are all at equilibrium; for water 273.16 K and 4.58 Torr. If it lies above atmospheric pressure no liquid is seen and the solid sublimes, as CO₂ does on Earth.

concepts.name: Standard and normal transition points
concepts.statement: The melting, boiling and sublimation points are where a line of constant pressure crosses the coexistence curves: at 1 bar the standard points, at 1 atm the normal ones.

concepts.name: Phases and dimensions in a phase diagram
concepts.statement: In a unary phase diagram a plane holds one phase, a curve two and a point three: the dimension and the number of phases always add up to three.

concepts.name: Moles exchanged between two phases
concepts.statement: When a pure substance only changes phase, its total amount is fixed: n_ice + n_water = n_total, so dn_ice = −dn_water.

concepts.name: Molar quantity
concepts.statement: An extensive function divided by the amount, G_molar = G/n and V_molar = V/n, written with a bar; the scaling assumes the function is a straight line through the origin in n.

concepts.name: Partial molar quantity
concepts.statement: In a mixture an extensive function need not be linear in each amount, so its partial molar value is its derivative with respect to one amount with the others fixed, V_partial molar,1 = ∂V/∂n₁ at constant n₂; it depends on composition, temperature and, less, pressure.

concepts.name: Chemical potential of a pure substance
concepts.statement: For a pure substance, in whatever phase, μ = (∂G/∂n)_{P,T} = G/n, the molar Gibbs energy Ḡ.

concepts.name: Ehrenfest classification of phase transitions
concepts.statement: A transition's order is the order of the first derivative of G to go discontinuous: in a first-order transition G has a kink, H, S and V jump and C_P, α and κ are singular; in a second-order one G is smooth, H and S have a kink and C_P jumps.

concepts.name: Second-order transition
concepts.statement: A transition in which G and its first derivatives H and S are continuous (with a kink) and only the second derivatives such as C_P are discontinuous, as in the order–disorder transition of paramagnetic materials.

concepts.name: The liquid has more entropy than the solid
concepts.statement: Since S = −∂G/∂T and the G(T) line of the liquid is steeper than the solid's, S(liquid) > S(solid); the same argument puts the gas above the liquid.

concepts.name: Molar volumes from the slopes of G against P
concepts.statement: Since V̄ = ∂Ḡ/∂P, the slopes of the Ḡ(P) segments give V̄(gas) ≫ V̄(liquid) > V̄(solid) for a normal substance such as benzene, and V̄(gas) ≫ V̄(solid) > V̄(liquid) for water, whose solid is less dense than its liquid.

concepts.name: Gibbs energy against pressure across the phases
concepts.statement: How Ḡ(P) changes with T: below the triple point the liquid curve is disconnected and the solid goes straight to gas; at the triple point all three meet; near the critical temperature only the liquid–gas break is left; above it a single supercritical fluid curve.

concepts.name: Conjugate variables
concepts.statement: Each form of work enters G as a pair of an intensive and an extensive variable, PV, ℰe, MH, FL, γA and μn, the product appearing in the state function and one times the change of the other in its differential.

concepts.name: Gibbs energy with other forms of work
concepts.statement: With electrical, magnetic, elastic and surface work, dG = −SdT + VdP + ℰde + MdH + FdL + γdA, and G = U + PV − TS + ℰe + MH + FL + γA + ….

concepts.name: Equal chemical potentials at phase equilibrium
concepts.statement: At constant T and P, dG = μ_ice dn_ice + μ_water dn_water with dn_ice = −dn_water, so 0 = Δμ dn_water and Δμ = 0: any two phases in equilibrium have the same chemical potential.

concepts.name: Change of the chemical potential with T and P
concepts.statement: As μ = Ḡ, (∂μ/∂P)_T = V̄ and (∂μ/∂T)_P = −S̄, so dμ = V̄dP − S̄dT for each phase.

concepts.name: Clapeyron equation
concepts.statement: Along a coexistence curve dμ is the same in both phases, so dP/dT = ΔS̄/ΔV̄ = ΔH̄/(TΔV̄): the slope of every phase boundary is set by the molar enthalpy and volume changes of the transition. For ice, ΔV̄ of melting is negative, so the melting line leans back.

concepts.name: Clausius–Clapeyron equation
concepts.statement: For a vapor equilibrium V̄_gas ≫ V̄_liquid and, if the vapor is ideal, V̄_gas = RT/P, so the Clapeyron equation becomes d ln P/dT = ΔH_vap/RT².

concepts.name: Integrated Clausius–Clapeyron equation
concepts.statement: With ΔH_vap independent of T, ln P = −ΔH_vap/RT + C, so ln(P₂/P₁) = −(ΔH_vap/R)(1/T₂ − 1/T₁): a vapor pressure at one temperature and ΔH_vap give it at any other, and ln P against 1/T is a straight line of slope −ΔH_vap/R.

concepts.name: Enthalpy of vaporization
concepts.statement: The molar enthalpy (heat) of vaporization, ΔH_vap, the enthalpy taken up when a mole of liquid becomes vapor; it varies slightly with temperature.

concepts.name: Vapor pressure rises with temperature
concepts.statement: The vaporization curves of most liquids have similar shapes, the vapor pressure rising steadily and faster than linearly with temperature; where a curve crosses 1 atm is the liquid's normal boiling point.

concepts.name: Enthalpy of sublimation
concepts.statement: The Clausius–Clapeyron equation applies to sublimation too, and the heat of sublimation is the sum of the heats of melting and vaporization.

concepts.name: Using the Clausius–Clapeyron equation
concepts.statement: Estimating a vapor pressure at another temperature from one vapor pressure and ΔH_vap, or the heat of a transition from the vapor pressures at two temperatures, keeping the order of the temperatures consistent; the Clapeyron equation, not this one, serves for melting.

concepts.name: Helmholtz energy from the partition function
concepts.statement: With U and S written through ln Q, A = U − TS gives A = −RT ln Q.

concepts.name: Chemical potential from the Helmholtz energy
concepts.statement: Comparing dG = dA + d(PV) with the fundamental equation for G shows μ = (∂G/∂n)_{P,T} = (∂A/∂n)_{V,T}: each potential gives μ with its own natural variables held constant.

concepts.name: Chemical potential from the partition function
concepts.statement: Putting A = −RT ln Q into μ = (∂A/∂n)_{V,T} gives μ = −RT(∂ln Q/∂n)_{V,T}.
